We show that, with dense transmission attempts, risk is primarily governed by loss persistence beyond the modeled memory, and the worst-case channel need not be the most persistent one. Under limited budgets, retry spacing makes loss relapse probabilities important and can reverse the risk ordering of compatible channels. Numerical and measurement results show that low-order models can substantially underestimate the risk, highlighting the need for scheduling-dependent channel statistics.

papers.title: Unital qubit channels are $3$-noisy
papers.abstract: The algebraic and environmental characteristics of mixed unitary quantum operations are investigated. It is established that the composition of two uniformly n-mixed unitary channels is itself n-noisy, and this n-noisy property is shown to be an invariant under unitary equivalence. Furthermore, by utilizing majorization and the divisibility of Kraus rank-four unital qubit channels, we demonstrate that any unital qubit channel can be physically simulated using a three-dimensional maximally mixed environment. Together, these results advance the classification and physical realization of noisy quantum channels.

papers.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring on Structured Graph Classes: Bounds, Exact Algorithms, and Hardness
papers.abstract: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper vertex coloring in which every non-isolated vertex has a neighbor whose color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood. We study this coloring on chordal and ordered bipartite graph classes. For well-partitioned chordal graphs, we prove the tight bound $ω(G)\leq\pcf(G)\leqω(G)+1$ and give an $O(n^2)$ construction from a partition tree. Every assignment of lists of at least $ω(G)+1$ colors also admits a PCF coloring that respects the lists. Deciding whether $ω(G)$ colors suffice is NP-complete, even when the partition tree is a star. This also proves NP-completeness on chordal graphs when the number of colors is part of the input. For interval graphs, we prove that lists of size $ω(G)+1$ always suffice, improving the previous ordinary-coloring bound of $ω(G)+2$. We use matchings to characterize when $ω(G)$ colors suffice and give an endpoint algorithm taking $2^{O(ω(G)^2)}n^{O(1)}$ time. We also characterize the exact value when the clique number is at most three and give a linear-time algorithm from sorted interval endpoints. For biconvex graphs, we prove a tight five-color bound and give a direct exact algorithm taking $O(n^{33})$ time. For bipartite permutation graphs, a smaller dynamic program gives an exact $O(n^{17})$ algorithm. Finally, if a bipartite graph is convex over an ordered shore $X$, we prove the sharp bound $\pcf(G)\leq\lceil\log_2(|X|+1)\rceil+3$ and construct a coloring in linear time from the order.

papers.title: The Complexity of KKT Points of Quadratic Programs with Polynomially-Bounded Coefficients
papers.abstract: Computing a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) point of a quadratic polynomial over the unit hypercube is known to be $CLS$-complete, when the coefficients of the polynomial are encoded in binary. We prove that the problem remains $CLS$-complete even when the coefficients are encoded in unary. This is the first problem proven to remain $CLS$-hard when the input is given in unary.

papers.title: Mixing Time of the Random-Pair Monte Shuffle
papers.abstract: In the random-pair Monte shuffle on $n$ cards, each step chooses two positions independently and uniformly and exchanges their cards with probability $1/2$. The chosen positions are public; the decisions to exchange cards remain hidden. We prove that the mixing time in expected conditional total variation distance is $2n\log n+O(n)$, with an exact leading constant and an $O(n)$ cutoff window. To our knowledge, this is the first public-schedule Monte shuffle whose full-permutation mixing time has been determined up to an additive $O(n)$ term. The upper bound follows by comparing two executions with the same public schedule to a classical random-transposition walk. For the lower bound, we construct a schedule-dependent test function and estimate its variance using a matrix-averaging operator. Combined with the depth bound of Czumaj and Lingas, the mixing estimate gives public switching networks with at most $2n\log n+O(n)$ switches and $O(\log n)$ depth for fixed error and failure probabilities. The author obtained this result through interaction with GPT-6 Astra.

papers.title: On the optimality of truncation among binary linear sketches
papers.abstract: We study statistical inference and function evaluation problems in which the input binary vector is available only through a binary linear sketch, i.e., a fixed number of parity measurements. We show that under a certain monotonicity condition, simply truncating the input by retaining a subset of its coordinates is optimal among all linear sketches of the same size. In particular, this applies to distributed testing of correlations of binary vectors when they are of opposite signs and evaluating unate Boolean functions on uniformly random inputs. Additionally, given that truncation is optimal, we immediately have lower bounds for arbitrary binary linear sketches. To illustrate this application, we consider the one-way communication complexity of a distributional graph connectivity problem on $n$ vertices and show that truncation, and hence all binary linear sketches, requires $Θ(n \log n)$ bits to achieve constant error, while a nonlinear protocol only requires $O(\log n)$ bits.

papers.title: A Review of Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control Algorithms: State of the Art and Research Opportunities
papers.abstract: Max-Pressure (MP) has emerged as a widely studied decentralized traffic signal control framework, thanks to its desirable theoretical properties and strong control performance. Early research on MP focused on improving control performance by exploring different variables of the traffic state for the definition of pressure. Subsequent studies expanded MP to incorporate the complexity of real-world transportation systems and emerging technologies. This paper provides a comprehensive review of these developments. The review first introduces the theoretical foundations of MP and examines early developments in movement weight definition. It then synthesizes major extensions for multimodal and multiscale network control, followed by recent developments in connected and automated vehicle (CAV) environments and the integration of MP with artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven methods. Beyond summarizing existing approaches, this review examines their underlying assumptions, data requirements, implementation considerations, and practical limitations. Based on this comprehensive review, key research gaps and future directions are identified, including remaining limitations in the theoretical foundations of MP and the underexplored integration of autonomous vehicle control with the MP framework. Overall, this review provides a structured perspective on the evolution and current state of MP control and highlights opportunities for developing more proactive, robust, and practically deployable MP-based traffic control methods.

papers.title: StreamLTT: Risk Certification for Policy Selection under Stream Dependence
papers.abstract: Learn-then-Test (LTT) provides a general framework for certifying deployment policies against a prescribed risk target, but its standard formulation targets a fixed population risk estimated from calibration losses. In sequential deployment, losses may instead be dependent and nonstationary, so the risk of a fixed policy can evolve with the observed history. We introduce StreamLTT, which replaces this fixed population risk with average predictable risk, defined by conditioning each decision's loss on the information available before its outcome is revealed. Conditional centering turns empirical deviations from this target into a martingale sum, enabling both a test that adapts to predictable variance and a finite-sample Hoeffding alternative. Combined with family-wise error rate control, StreamLTT yields a simultaneously certified policy region that supports subsequent deployment selection. Across seven forecasting datasets and seven deployment risks, StreamLTT places the certified frontier substantially closer to the prescribed risk target than IID, robust-variance, block-bootstrap, and concentration-based alternatives, while empirical family-wise error closely follows the prescribed level. A finite-sample ablation further shows that the predictable-risk formulation drives the tighter risk frontier, while adaptation to predictable variance makes more effective use of the available family-wise error budget. StreamLTT therefore extends risk-certified policy selection to dependent deployment streams by addressing both what risk should be certified and how it should be tested.

papers.title: Time to AC-t: When AC-transmission changes capacity expansion planning
papers.abstract: Capacity expansion models often dramatically simplify the physics of how power flows through a transmission network in order to preserve computational tractability. However, with the rapid growth of electrification, large loads, renewables, and storage, increased realism in planning future grids is imperative. We extend the open-source capacity expansion model GenX with AC optimal power flow physics, and analyze generation, storage, and transmission investment decisions for 20-zone, hourly models of Germany and Texas. We compare our results against those using two common approximations, the transport model and DC optimal power flow. We find that total costs and emissions largely agree across all formulations. However, we find substantial differences in outputs related to transmission, generation siting, storage, and reactive-power support between the approximate formulations and the true AC physics formulation. We identify where AC physics changes planning decisions and discuss how to potentially capture these effects without the full computational cost.
papers.comments: 35 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables; plus 16 pages of supplemental information (8 figures, 6 tables). Submitted to Joule

papers.title: On the Role of Geometry in Solving Variational Inequalities
papers.abstract: The geometry of constraints in variational inequalities (VIs) plays a central role in applications ranging from resource allocation and equilibrium computation to constrained optimization. Yet, its effect on computational complexity has received surprisingly little attention beyond special cases. We examine this question when the constraint set is an $\ell_p$ ball. This family of problems encompasses two of the most extensively studied classes of problems in algorithmic game theory: symmetric bimatrix games for $p = 1$ and multi-player polymatrix games for $p = \infty$. Both of these problems are known to be PPAD-complete even for affine operators. We establish a comprehensive complexity landscape for VIs over $\ell_p$ balls across the full range $p\in[1,\infty]$. First, for any $p\neq 2$, we show that finding an inverse-polynomial approximate VI solution is PPAD-complete even for affine operators. In contrast, for $p=2$, we give a polynomial-time algorithm for affine VIs, extending a classic result of Ye (1992) beyond symmetric operators. On the other hand, once the operator becomes quadratic, we establish PPAD-completeness even at inverse polynomial precision. From a technical standpoint, we develop a new toolkit for exploiting the geometry of the constraint set and the structure of the operator to characterize the complexity of equilibrium and optimization problems, which is of independent interest.

papers.title: Nonparametric GARCH: An Iterated Neural Estimator
papers.abstract: We study nonparametric estimation and forecasting for GARCH-type processes and propose an iterated neural estimator that alternates between estimating the recursion map and updating the unobserved conditional variances. Under mild conditions, we establish finite-sample bounds for the time-averaged in-sample variance-path error and show that the estimator is minimax rate-optimal up to logarithmic factors. Under stationarity and mixing conditions, we establish the same rate for recursion-map estimation and derive finite-sample bounds for out-of-sample variance forecasts and expected excess Gaussian quasi-likelihood (QLIKE) loss. The convergence rates depend on the true lag orders and remain unchanged when the fitted orders are overspecified. Simulation studies illustrate the effectiveness of our estimators under nonlinear and time-varying volatility dynamics. Real-data applications suggest that our neural methods perform competitively and can incorporate option-price and high-frequency information.

papers.title: Point interpolation and distributional universality in flow-based generative models
papers.abstract: Motivated by the expressive power of neural ordinary differential equations in flow-based generative modeling, we study the approximation of probability measures by pushforwards generated by parameterized families of Lipschitz vector fields. For Wasserstein distances, we establish a quantitative relationship between finite-sample point interpolation and distributional approximation, and derive universality criteria based on $L^p$-approximation of transport maps. In particular, affine-invariant families containing a non-affine vector field are universal from compactly supported absolutely continuous base measures. For total variation, we show that coordinate-wise dynamics are insufficient in dimensions $d\geq 2$ and establish sufficient conditions based on one-dimensional Sobolev approximation and shear-type mixing. We further examine the role of point interpolation, establishing when different regimes relate to one another and when approximate interpolation can be made exact.

papers.title: Testing Implies Distance Estimation with Polynomial Loss
papers.abstract: A tester decides whether a graph has a property or is far from having it. A distance estimator asks for more: it must approximately determine how many edges need to be changed. A property is said to be testable if there is a tester with a number of queries bounded independently of the graph's order for each conceivable distance. Similarly, if a property admits an estimator with a number of queries bounded independently of the graph's order, it is said to be estimable. Fischer and Newman proved that, in the dense graph model, every testable property is also estimable. We show that the passage from testing to estimation requires only a polynomial increase in query complexity. This resolves a long-standing open problem in property testing, previously tackled by Fiat and Ron, by Hoppen, Kohayakawa, Lang, Lefmann, and Stagni, and by Gishboliner, Kushnir, and Shapira.

papers.title: Inferential Issues in Model-based Small Area Estimation: Some History and Selective Recent Advances
papers.abstract: Model-based Small Area Estimation (SAE) has seen rapid growth over the past 25 years or so due to the rapidly increasing demand for reliable small area estimators of totals, means and more complex area parameters. Direct area-specific estimators are either unreliable (due to small area-specific sample sizes) or not feasible (due to zero area-specific sample sizes). It is therefore necessary to borrow strength from related areas through implicit or explicit models linking related areas. We focus on explicit area-level and unit-level models. After a brief historical sketch of the evolution of SAE, we focus on selective recent developments (mostly after 2015). Developments before 2015 are mostly covered in the comprehensive Wiley book by Rao and Molina (2015). Under a basic area-level model, we consider semi-parametric and robust estimation of small area means under model misspecifications. Under a basic unit level model, methods for estimating complex parameters, such as poverty indicators, will be presented, including robust estimation in the presence of outliers. A comparison of area-level and unit-level models when unit level data are available will also be presented. Estimation methods studied include empirical best linear unbiased prediction (EBLUP), empirical best (EB) and hierarchical Bayes (HB).

papers.title: An example of universal braiding in Links--Gould topological quantum computation
papers.abstract: We construct a universal quantum computational encoding via braiding in Links--Gould fusion spaces associated to $U_q^H(\mathfrak{sl}(2|1))$ where $q$ is on the unit circle and is not a root of unity. The construction uses only neglectons and is realized in the morphism spaces $\mathrm{Hom}_{U_q^H}(V(0,α),V(0,-\frac{1}{2})^{\otimes 2N}\otimes V(0,α)).$ Under explicit positivity and arithmetic constraints these spaces admit a $2^N$-dimensional computational subspace with a positive definite Hermitian form. We prove single-qubit density in $\mathrm{U}(2,1)$ and approximate arbitrary unitary operators on $N$-qubit computational subspaces with arbitrarily small leakage. The calculations use explicit inclusions, projections, and Hermitian pairings without requiring $F$-matrices.

papers.title: How Risky Is Your Data-Driven Policy?
papers.abstract: Data-driven algorithms are ubiquitous across industries, and there is an extensive literature on analyzing their \emph{average} performance. The risk profile of such algorithms, while critical, is much less understood. This paper quantifies the risk of data-driven policies and isolates its sources. We evaluate a policy through the conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of its loss over the training sample, any policy randomization, and the future outcome, at a fixed unknown distribution. Regret against an oracle that knows the distribution decomposes into expected post-sample regret (PS), the average outcome-only CVaR gap of the selected action, and a sample-risk premium (SR), the additional tail risk omitted by averaging those evaluations. The analogous premium vanishes under expected loss. We characterize when the premium vanishes and how large it is relative to post-sample regret. For losses with a continuous density near the tail cutoff, we identify conditions under which both components decay at the same rate, yet the limiting ratio of the premium to post-sample regret can reach the thousands. When a probability mass at the cutoff moves with the action, the premium can decay more slowly and dominate post-sample regret. We establish conditions under which sample average approximation learns the oracle action at rate $n^{-1/2}$ in both settings, but its combined-risk regret is of order $n^{-1}$ in the first and $n^{-1/2}$ in the second. In finite-sample numerical examples of SAA in both settings, the premium accounts for approximately $74\%$--$97\%$ of regret.

papers.title: State Evolution and Universality of Iterated Linear Programs for the Binary Perceptron
papers.abstract: The binary perceptron is a random constraint satisfaction problem that asks for a sign vector satisfying a system of random linear inequalities. Its solution space has a strikingly extreme geometry: at every positive constraint density, all but a vanishing fraction of the solutions are isolated. Yet polynomial-time algorithms find solutions at small enough constraint density, which raises the question of how efficient algorithms navigate such a landscape. Linear programming is a natural algorithm to study here, but its analysis has so far been limited to a single round. Li, Schramm, and Zhou (STOC 2025) analyzed one linear program followed by iterative rounding. In this work, we overcome this limitation and give a precise analysis of iterated linear programming for the binary perceptron. (1) For Gaussian matrices and any fixed number of rounds, we characterize the iterated linear programs exactly through a deterministic state-evolution recursion. (2) Adding a final rounding step, we obtain a randomized polynomial-time algorithm for the binary perceptron. Numerical evaluations of the recursion provide evidence that it succeeds at constraint density $α=0.60$ with zero margin, well beyond the range $α\le0.1$ guaranteed by the single-LP analysis and $α\approx0.327$ (Jo and Lee, 2026), the best guarantee so far. (3) We establish universality, showing that the same characterization holds for matrices with i.i.d. entries drawn from any centered, unit-variance subgaussian law. The key idea of our proof is that, although conditioning on earlier rounds makes the matrix non-Gaussian, its conditional law can be computed explicitly and remains close to a Gaussian law, so the convex Gaussian min-max theorem applies in every round. For universality, we compare Gaussian and subgaussian matrices through the Lindeberg principle, using a regularized version of each linear program.

papers.title: Approximate Synthetic Spectra of Quantum Systems Associated with Compact Lie Groups
papers.abstract: How can noncommuting quantum observables retain the geometry of a classical phase space? Motivated by Mumford's question on approximately macroscopically unique (AMU) states and the work of Lin and Wang, we study synthetic spectra of position--momentum and angular-momentum systems. Under the hypotheses of their AMU theorems, nonempty synthetic spectra yield AMU states. For sufficiently small $\hbar$, the position--momentum spectrum fills the plane, while the angular-momentum spectrum contains any prescribed ball. The latter calculation leads to compact Lie groups: we prove that highest-weight coadjoint orbits lie in regional synthetic spectra under an explicit variance bound. Function-space representations of $SU(n)$, $SO(n)$, and $Sp(n)$ provide further examples.

papers.title: Computing Invariant Reachable Sets through Sum-of-Squares Programming
papers.abstract: Funnels, time-varying invariant sets around nominal trajectories, certify that a closed-loop system tracks its plan, and can be composed into verified motion plans. Their computation by sum-of-squares (SOS) programming is well established in formulation but not in practice: the result depends on implementation choices such as the initial guess, Lyapunov function normalization, and termination rule, which the literature documents only briefly. This paper presents a self-contained treatment of SOS-based funnel computation, implemented in the open-source package computeSOSFunnels. We propose a minimum-volume formulation with inlet and outlet constraints under which funnels with coinciding nominal endpoints compose by construction. Numerical experiments on a unicycle, with timing studies on a cart-pole and a 12-state quadrotor, characterize the pipeline: infeasible initial guesses are partly decidable before solving, the certificate shows no violations among 39,000 boundary samples per funnel under the true dynamics, and constructing the semidefinite program, not solving it, dominates computation time.
papers.comments: 8 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology. Code: github.com/khalid2696/computeSOSFunnels

papers.title: A Conditional Quantum Kac-Bernstein Theorem
papers.abstract: We establish a conditional quantum Kac-Bernstein theorem for mixing of two independent, finite-mode bosonic inputs with quantum memories. We characterize exactly when the outputs are conditionally independent given both memories. Each input then decomposes into orthogonal memory sectors sharing a common Gaussian state on the physical system and a bosonic memory factor, up to sector-dependent physical displacements. In particular, triviality of the common bosonic factor implies separability of the inputs, as occurs whenever either memory has finite-dimensional support.

papers.title: Competition, Switching, and Control in Coupled Adoption-Opinion Dynamics
papers.abstract: We propose a Multi-technology AdopTion-opinion co-Evolution (MATE) model to describe the diffusion of $m \geq 2$ competing alternatives within a networked population whose opinions evolve under social influence and the feedback generated by adoption. Communities interact through two layers: a physical network governing exposure to adoption, and a social network shaping opinion evolution through social imitation. Individuals can adopt a technology, eventually becoming dissatisfied at a rate reflecting the quality of the technology, and switch to an alternative at a rate driven by their opinion of that alternative. For an arbitrary number of competing technologies $m \geq 2$, we characterize the equilibria and establish the existence of an adoption-diffused equilibrium in which all technologies coexist. For $m > 2$, the equilibrium configuration depends on the broader competitive environment: unlike the two-technology case, within-community relative adoption generally depends also on equilibrium opinions and on the other alternatives. Finally, we formulate finite-horizon opinion-shaping control problems, derive necessary optimality conditions via the discrete-time Pontryagin maximum principle, and compute numerical extremals using a forward-backward sweep method.

papers.title: Binary Huffman Coding with Unequal Letter Costs Is NP-Complete
papers.abstract: Binary prefix coding assigns prefix-free binary words to symbols to minimize their frequency-weighted cost. Huffman solved the equal-letter-cost case in polynomial time in 1952 [Proc. IRE'52]. For unequal letter costs, Karp gave an integer-programming formulation in 1961 [IRE Trans. Inf. Theory'61]. Exact polynomial-time algorithms for fixed integer costs were given by Golin and Rote [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory'98] and Bradford, Golin, Larmore, and Rytter [J. Algorithms'02]. For input-dependent costs, Golin, Mathieu, and Young gave a polynomial-time approximation scheme [SICOMP'12]. The exact complexity when letter costs are part of the input had remained unresolved. We resolve this $65$-year-old problem by proving that deciding whether there exists a binary prefix-free code of frequency-weighted cost at most a given threshold is NP-complete, even when the letter costs are consecutive positive integers $(M,M+1)$ supplied as part of the input. All frequencies, letter costs, and thresholds are encoded in binary. Consequently, finding an optimal code is NP-hard. Our proof uses two polynomial-time reductions, starting from Planar Independent Set. The intermediate problem prescribes the number of leaves at each depth of a full ordered binary tree and minimizes a signed linear score on their sorted right-edge counts. The first reduction represents an independent-set verification program by a tree growing level by level. A fixed-profile identity converts narrow coordinate restrictions into linear penalties that enforce the computation. The second reduction adds large dyadic terms to the symbol frequencies to force prescribed depths. These terms contribute a constant to the weighted number of ones, leaving smaller signed perturbations to reproduce the tree score.

papers.title: On the IQC and SRG Frameworks: Equivalences and Converse Results
papers.abstract: Integral quadratic constraints (IQCs) and scaled relative graphs (SRGs) are two prominent frameworks for analyzing feedback systems. Although both frameworks are rooted in the same graph separation principle, a general characterization of their relationship has remained unavailable. This paper establishes conditions under which the IQC- and SRG frameworks are equivalent. To this end, we introduce two new classes of systems, termed disjunctive and conjunctive systems, which are respectively characterized by unions and intersections of quadratic input-output constraints. Under structural assumptions, we prove equivalence between the IQC and SRG frameworks for these system classes. By exploiting this equivalence, we develop novel IQC- and SRG-based converse stability results for linear and nonlinear systems. Our results accommodate multiple quadratic constraints, extending well-known converse results in robust control beyond the single-constraint setting.

papers.title: Decentralized Sparse Quantile Regression
papers.abstract: Distributed statistical learning has recently attracted significant attention owing to its computational efficiency and scalability in large-scale systems. However, the non-smooth quantile loss poses substantial challenges to the development of efficient decentralized algorithms for quantile regression. Existing methods may either suffer from slow convergence or rely on smoothing-based approximations that require additional stringent assumptions, particularly in high-dimensional settings. To address these issues, we propose a decentralized framework that integrates gradient tracking with iterative hard thresholding for sparse quantile estimation. The proposed method avoids smoothing approximations and relaxes the initialization requirement. Theoretically, we show that the proposed algorithm achieves linear convergence under stated regularity conditions and that the resulting estimator attains the same order of statistical accuracy as its centralized counterpart. We further develop a decentralized information criterion for selecting the working sparsity level and establish support screening guarantees. Numerical experiments and a real-data study illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed method.

papers.title: Lower Bounds for Adaptive Relaxed Locally Decodable Codes via the Capped Horvitz--Thompson Estimator
papers.abstract: We prove a nearly optimal lower bound on the blocklength of general relaxed locally decodable codes (RLDCs), extending the result of [GGS26] to nonlinear encodings and adaptive decoders with two-sided error. Namely, we show that any $q$-query RLDC $C\colon \{0,1\}^k \to \{0,1\}^n$ must satisfy $n = k^{1+Ω(1/q)}$, closely matching the upper bound of $n = k^{1+O(1/q)}$ by Ben-Sasson, Goldreich, Harsha, Sudan, and Vadhan (STOC 2004). Our proof reduces showing RLDC lower bounds to estimating the output distribution of adaptive decoders. To this end, we introduce a capped Horvitz--Thompson estimator with uniformly bounded discrete derivatives on the $p$-biased cube. We establish its concentration of measure via self-bounding inequalities and control the downward bias induced by capping through a spreadness argument.

papers.title: Glauber Dynamics for Sampling Colorings: Rapid Mixing above $(1+1/\mathrm{e})Δ$ via Hidden Hard-Core Models
papers.abstract: We show that for every $γ>0$ and every sufficiently large $Δ$, the Glauber dynamics for proper $q$-colorings of any $n$-vertex graph of maximum degree $Δ$ has spectral gap $Ω_γ(1/n)$, and hence mixing time $O_γ(n^2\log q)$, whenever $q\ge(1+1/\mathrm{e}+γ)Δ$. Our proof establishes a Bochner-type inequality by exploiting the spectral gaps of hard-core models hidden in the color classes. The constant $1+1/\mathrm{e}\approx1.368$ comes from the uniqueness threshold $\approx\mathrm{e}/Δ$ of the hard-core model on the infinite $Δ$-regular tree.

papers.title: Real-Space renormalization for the drawups and drawdowns of stochastic trajectories: universality classes for diffusion processes and random walks via the scale function
papers.abstract: For one-dimensional diffusion processes with arbitrary diffusion coefficient $D(x)$ and Ito force $F_I(x)$, we analyze the statistical properties of the renormalized trajectories at scale $Γ$, where one keeps only the alternating sequence of local minima and local maxima that are separated by drawups and drawdowns of amplitude bigger than $Γ$. The elementary RG-step between $Γ$ and $Γ+d Γ$ thus amounts to eliminate the drawups and drawdowns of amplitude $Γ$, a real-space-RG-procedure that is well-known for Brownian trajectories in the context of the Strong-Disorder-RG approach applied to the disorder landscape of random models. The main result is that the universality classes are determined by the scale function $s(x)$ satisfying $D(x) s''(x)+F_I(x) s'(x)=0$ that governs the exit probabilities from an interval : all the diffusions sharing the same scale function $s(x)$ have the same statistics of renormalized trajectories, even if their initial microscopic trajectories are completely different. The simplest universality classes for diffusions on the whole line $x \in ]-\infty,+\infty[$ and on the half-line $x \in ]0,+\infty[$ are illustrated with several examples of processes, with or without steady states: Cauchy, Student, Bessel, Fisher-Snedecor, Geometric Brownian. This framework concerning diffusion processes is then adapted to discrete-time and to continuous-time random walks on the one-dimensional lattice with arbitrary nearest-neighbor jump probabilities or rates.

papers.title: The Nonlinear Physics and Statistical Field Theory of Twilight Clouds: Hovering Dynamics and Dynamic Inertia Emergence
papers.abstract: Twilight clouds are small, optically faint warm clouds whose droplets fluctuate between haze and activated growth. We develop a nonequilibrium statistical field theory linking this regime to cloud-field organization through Köhler microphysics, supersaturation transport, and turbulent mixing. At parcel level, supersaturation rapidly tracks slow droplet growth with a finite lag. Mixing-induced supersaturation removal drives a saddle-node bifurcation, shifting the activation threshold and supporting intermittent hovering under turbulent fluctuations. Starting from turbulent transport of supersaturation coupled to droplet growth, we derive a droplet-supersaturation field system and formulate it within the Martin-Siggia-Rose framework. A Gurari-type variational reduction inspired by polaron theory eliminates the fast bath. Turbulence dresses the slow droplet field, shrinks the forbidden zone below the equilibrium curve, and raises the mixing threshold required to suppress activation. Each droplet population induces a screened supersaturation halo that couples neighboring cloud elements; its delayed adjustment generates dynamic inertia and temporally correlated noise. The resulting nonlinear, non-Markovian pseudoparabolic stochastic equation has a bounded frozen-background response at short wavelengths. Its long-wave coupling amplifies contrasts where the dressed slow manifold turns downward. Comparisons with the parent two-field system show that a spatially correlated Markovian closure preserves droplet-radius distributions and cloudlet organization. Near the activation fold, restoring residual-bath fluctuation memory improves recurrent-hovering frequency and patch extent without recalibrating the drift or fitting a correlation time. More broadly, the framework identifies how slow fields acquire interactions and inertia through the relaxing, diffusive environments they modify.

papers.title: Deep Neural Operator Learning for stochastic heat equations and applications
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a universal approximation theorem for solution operators of semilinear stochastic heat equations in spatial dimension \(d\ge2\), extending deep neural operator approximation results to SPDEs with distribution-valued Gaussian forcing. A smooth Fourier cutoff reduces the forcing to finitely many measurements, while Besov and Schauder estimates control the resulting solution error. The finite-dimensional solution map is then approximated by ReLU branch networks together with grid-based trunk functions, yielding explicit bounds on the numbers of forcing measurements and trunk functions and approximation in every finite stochastic moment. For linear equations, the reduction coincides with truncation of the first Wiener chaos. Lastly, as an application, we prove a high-probability local-in-time approximation theorem for stochastic Navier--Stokes equations, with finite measurements of both the initial condition and forcing and an explicit sensing rate.

papers.title: Substantially Improved Rate and Distance for Addressable Transversal Phase Gates
papers.abstract: An important ingredient in fault-tolerant quantum computation is asymptotically good codes with fully addressable transversal non-Clifford gates. Existing constructions, however, provide only small explicit guarantees for rate and relative distance. Here, we substantially improve these guarantees for fully addressable transversal phase gates at every fixed level $h\ge3$ of the Clifford hierarchy, using a cyclic encoding beyond the binary CSS framework. The encoding separates logical phase control from the joint design of rate and distance, enabling two constructions with different computational costs. A deterministic polynomial-time algebraic-geometric construction gives a common asymptotic lower bound of $52/(675h)$ on both quantities. A counting argument gives an exponential-time construction with exact verification, improving this bound by a factor of approximately $2.86$. We further establish a universal upper bound for codes supporting fully addressable transversal single-qubit phase gates. Within our cyclic encoding framework, we obtain a stronger upper bound that is approximately $1.28$ times the lower bound achieved by our exponential-time construction. As concrete examples, we construct codes with $48$ and $90$ physical qubits supporting fully addressable transversal $T$ gates. These results narrow the gap between achievable code parameters and addressability bounds, providing quantitative targets for further improvements in efficient code constructions.

papers.title: Basic Reproductive Numbers in Host-Parasite Systems with Demographic Bistability
papers.abstract: The basic reproductive number, $\mathcal{R}_0$, is widely used to determine whether an infectious disease can persist in a population. However, its interpretation may become unclear when the underlying disease-free demographic dynamics exhibit multiple types of stable attractors. In this study, we investigate how demographic bistability between fixed points and periodic cycles affects the calculation and interpretation of $\mathcal{R}_0$. We consider two discrete-time host-parasite models with infection: a tick-host model motivated by Borrelia burgdorferi transmission and a Nicholson-Bailey host-parasitoid model with intraspecific competition and infection. For each model, we calculate reproductive numbers associated with different disease-free attractors using the next-generation operator method and compare their invasion thresholds. In the tick-host model, the reproduction number calculated on the stable demographic cycle differs from that calculated at the positive coexistence fixed point, resulting in parameter regions where infection can invade at one demographic attractor but not the other. In contrast, in the host-parasitoid model, the host-driven invasion threshold is necessarily the same at the positive coexistence fixed point and on the host-only periodic cycles. These contrasting results demonstrate that demographic bistability alone does not necessarily produce attractor-dependent invasion thresholds. Rather, the effect of demographic dynamics on invasion depends on the structure of pathogen transmission. In particular, a complete host--vector--host transmission pathway can allow differences between demographic attractors to alter the invasion threshold. Our results emphasize the importance of considering both demographic dynamics and transmission structure when interpreting $\mathcal{R}_0$ in populations with multiple stable disease-free states.

papers.title: Hecke Relations from Self-Duality
papers.abstract: Hecke operators can be used to relate characters of rational conformal field theories with different central charges, but it has remained a mystery how to interpret these relations physically. We offer a simple explanation in terms of self-duality under asymmetric orbifolds. Self-dual orbifolds also give more general identities beyond the familiar Harvey-Wu construction, which we illustrate through examples.

papers.title: The integer spectrum of a superintegrable quantum field theory
papers.abstract: In our previous article CMP 407 (2026) 131, we explored the rich algebraic structures arising from a specific quantum many-body Hamiltonian quartic in the bosonic creation-annihilation operators. This Hamiltonian originated from the works of Gérard and Grellier on classical turbulent energy transfer in a Lax-integrable setting, and its quantum version respects hierarchies of polynomial conservation laws all of which possess purely integer spectra, as does the Hamiltonian itself. The latter feature, known from numerical studies, has previously remained unproved. Here, we present an elementary solution of the quantum Gérard-Grellier Hamiltonian. The eigenstates are labelled by partitions and the corresponding eigenvalues admit simple explicit expressions in terms of the principal hook lengths. The key ingredient in this construction is a specific basis we introduce, inspired by the classical multisoliton coherent states, in which the Hamiltonian is upper-triangular. The expressions for the eigenvalues then immediately follow, while the full eigenbasis can be recovered via a Gram-Schmidt procedure.

papers.title: Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle
papers.abstract: Matrix factorization provides a simple model for studying the training dynamics of neural networks. Recent studies of gradient flow under small initialization have analyzed how trajectories escape from a neighborhood of the origin and approach their first nonzero stationary point. In this paper, we study continuous-time dynamics that applies a finite number of Newton-Schulz iterations to the normalized matrix gradient (Muon). We show that the number of Newton-Schulz steps can change the rank selected during the early stages of training and allow the resulting trajectory to bypass the first nonzero stationary point approached by gradient flow. Under an additional residual-inertia condition, we prove that bypass occurs for all sufficiently large finite Newton-Schulz depths and provide an explicit sufficient threshold. We also construct an example in which the bypass threshold is four.

papers.title: Enabling risk and reliability analysis in next-generation computational tools via multifidelity methods
papers.abstract: Risk and reliability analysis are fundamental to the design, assessment, and operation of safety-critical complex systems; however, their integration into next-generation computational tools is constrained by the cost of uncertainty quantification with expensive computational models. The computational challenge is particularly prohibitive for tail-sensitive quantities, such as probabilities of failure, conditional values-at-risk, and buffered probabilities of failure, where accurate estimation can require a large number of model evaluations. Multifidelity methods provide a framework for addressing this computational bottleneck by combining information from models of varying accuracy and cost while retaining the predictive accuracy of the high-fidelity model. This review summarizes the state of the art in methods that enable scalable risk and reliability analysis using multifidelity control variates, multifidelity importance sampling, and multifidelity active learning.

papers.title: Beyond Multi-Index Models: Learning Intersections of Degree-2 PTFs
papers.abstract: We give an algorithm for PAC learning intersections of $k$ degree-2 polynomial threshold functions over $R^d$ under a Gaussian distribution. Our algorithm achieves classification error $ε$ using $d^{O(k)}2^{O_k(\log^3(1/ε))}$ time and samples, improving over the $d^{O(k^2/ε^2)}$ running time of the polynomial regression approach. To our knowledge, our result is the first to obtain a dimension exponent independent of the accuracy parameter, even for $k=2$. We complement our algorithmic result with an SQ lower bound showing that the complexity dependence of $d^{Ω(k)}$ is unavoidable. Lifting the input to polynomial features turns the target into an intersection of $k$ halfspaces. This suggests using the first two labeled moments for subspace recovery. In the lifted space, however, these moments can reveal nothing. Our starting point is a Gaussian comparison theorem showing that, for sufficiently regular defining quadratics, the labeled moments needed for subspace recovery are approximately preserved. To handle arbitrary defining quadratics, we establish a new structural result showing that every direction with significant resampling influence can be detected through degree-$O(k)$ moments. These results yield an initial $d^{O(k)}2^{\mathrm{poly}_k(1/ε)}$-time learner using adaptive restrictions. To improve the exponential dependence on $1/ε$, we develop a two-stage dimension-reduction approach that avoids the costly adaptive partitioning. After identifying a subspace containing all directions with large influence, we use generalized regularity and Gaussian comparison to recover the remaining relevant quadratic features through a new derivative-based moment operator. The recovered features support an intersection close to the target. Combining them with robust hinge-loss minimization gives our quasipolynomial-time learner.

papers.title: Do Ray-Traced Cities Make a Better Channel Prior for an Unseen Site? A Pre-Registered Study in Simulation, and a Test on Measured Channels that Reverses It
papers.abstract: Channel estimators at a newly deployed base station usually start from 3GPP stochastic channel models, which describe no particular street. We ask whether a channel prior pooled from many ray-traced cities serves an unseen site better than the 3GPP CDL models, and whether learned estimators make the difference. With Sionna RT on 14 city scenes, LMMSE estimation from covariance priors, leave-one-city-out evaluation, and pass/fail bars written down before each main experiment, we find in simulation that the pooled prior sits about 0.6 dB from a site-trained estimator with no site measurements, about what CDL reaches after 50 measurements. Learned models added little: at most 0.65 dB in estimation, and in channel prediction a simple classical method beat CNN predictors by 1.8-12 dB from 2 ms ahead. On measured channels from the DICHASUS outdoor dataset (1.272 GHz, three 2x8 arrays on one building) the result reversed: the pooled ray-traced prior was 3.2-4.1 dB worse than CDL. The simulated channels were too clean; with users at the real distances, even a scattering level tuned from 50 site measurements left the prior about 2 dB behind CDL. A pre-registered follow-on on two more measured environments found the generic CDL prior 2.1-4.7 dB from a site-trained one: no further in a factory hall than on the street, furthest in a small lab room. Finally, a hallway model calibrated to measurements by differentiable ray tracing reproduced delay spread, but as a prior in an unmeasured part of the hallway it was 4.5 dB worse than CDL on the full array. All measured results come from one sounder.

papers.title: A Random Matrix Analysis of Symmetric Tensor Unfolding
papers.abstract: We study a fundamental problem in machine learning: partial recovery of a planted signal $\boldsymbol{v} \in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ from a spiked tensor $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}} = λ\, \boldsymbol{v}^{\otimes p} + \boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$, where $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$ has symmetric Gaussian entries of variance $\asymp n^{-1}$. While previous works replace $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$ by an i.i.d. standard Gaussian tensor to circumvent technical difficulties caused by dependencies, this paper directly analyzes the symmetric model via random matrix theory. We show that the square unfolding algorithm is subject to a sharp phase transition for partial recovery at $λ\asymp n^{(p-2) / 4}$, validating an open conjecture from Montanari and Richard (2014). We get precise expressions for the limiting spectral distribution, deterministic equivalent, phase transition threshold and overlap. The main message is that unfolded symmetric tensors spectrally behave like standard Wigner matrices, up to simple transformations accounting for high-order symmetries. We consider extensions to multiple orthogonal spikes, recursive unfolding and non-square unfolding via disproportionate random matrix theory, leading to an interesting conjectured statistical-computational tradeoff regarding the choice of unfolding: square versus long.

papers.title: Path Decompositions of Sparse Graphs via Gaussian Sweeps and Faster Exponential Algorithms
papers.abstract: Using the bisection bound of Monien and Preis, Fomin and Høie proved in 2006 that every graph of maximum degree 3 on $n$ vertices has pathwidth at most $n/6+o(n)$. We prove that the pathwidth, bisection width and cutwidth of these graphs are at most $c_3 n+o(n)$, where $c_3=\frac{3}{4π}\arccos\frac56\approx0.1398$. For bisection width this improves the bound $n/6+o(n)$ of Monien and Preis (2006) and extends to all such graphs the bound that Lichev and Mitsche (2023) obtained for random cubic graphs. For maximum degree 4, we prove that bisection width and cutwidth are at most $n/3+o(n)$, improving the bound $2n/5+o(n)$ of Monien and Preis for 4-regular graphs, and that pathwidth is at most $0.2458n$, improving the bound $n/3$ of Fomin, Gaspers, Saurabh and Stepanov (2009). We show that every graph with $m$ edges has pathwidth at most $7m/48+o(n)$, improving the bound $13m/75$ of Scott and Sorkin (2007), and we give further bounds of the form $\sum_{d\ge3}a_d n_d+o(n)$ with $a_d<1$, where $n_d$ is the number of vertices of degree $d$. The path decompositions, and linear orderings of the stated cutwidth, can be computed in polynomial time. Instead of deriving pathwidth bounds from bisection width, we give each vertex a Gaussian label, a weighted sum of independent standard normal variables over a ball around it, and sweep a threshold through the labels; the bags are frontiers, the vertices above the threshold with a neighbor below it. We bound the probability that a vertex lies in a frontier by comparison with an explicit Gaussian model of a vertex and its neighbors. Faster exact algorithms follow: for feedback vertex set and the traveling salesperson problem on graphs of bounded maximum or average degree, and on general graphs for minimum weight dominating set (by branching until the instance is sparse), Max 2-CSP and counting subgraphs with $k$ edges (by the bound in $m$).
papers.comments: Code, computer certificates and Lean 4 formal proofs: https://serggasp.github.io/pathwidth-site/ and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23883489

papers.title: Ensembles of Random Partition-Based Models under Covariate Shift
papers.abstract: Distribution shifts, including covariate shifts, are ubiquitous in real-world applications of machine learning. Empirical evidence suggests that, across a variety of models with and without downstream adaptation, ensembles tend to be more robust to covariate shift than single models. We extend the theory of covariate shift severity from single models to ensembles, providing theoretical justification for the empirical trends. We introduce new discrepancy measures of covariate shift severity to control the risk of partition-based kernel estimators. We then show that with sufficient ensemble size, these models can achieve minimax-optimal risk convergence rates under covariate shift. Our results suggest that modelers can expect to need larger ensemble sizes for more severe covariate shifts.

papers.title: Regret-based Characterization, Information Limits, and the Sample Complexity of Auditing Adaptive Policies
papers.abstract: A policy can earn its performance by where it locates on average or by reacting to information. For any Markov policy $π$ in a finite-horizon MDP, let $ν$ be its open-loop marginal, which plays $π$'s average action distribution at each step. We show that $J(π)-J(ν)$ equals $\sum_t tr Cov(Q^ν_t,π_t)$ under endogenous dynamics. Audits based on immediate costs alone can have the wrong sign. Writing the covariance as a joint-versus-product gap gives the bound $|J(π)-J(ν)|\le\sum_t span_t\sqrt{I(s_t;a_t)/2}$, with a sharp constant. Hence, an MDP's adaptivity gap is bounded by the information that its optimal policy uses. Estimating $J(π)-J(ν)$ from $π$'s own bandit-feedback logs takes $Θ(\barχ^2 \log(1/η)/δ^2)$ rounds, where $\barχ^2$ is an average $χ^2$-divergence. At the same time, deterministic non-constant policies cannot be audited at all. We also provide an importance-sampling auditor for episodic MDPs.

papers.title: Beyond the Bochner Method: Optimal Spectral Gaps for Block Dynamics of Spin Systems like the $O(N)$ Model
papers.abstract: Let $μ$ be a probability distribution on a spin system with $n$ sites and possibly infinite spin spaces. We prove local-to-global spectral-gap bounds for block Glauber dynamics. Given a symmetric, entrywise nonnegative matrix $A$ with zero diagonal and $λ_{\max}(A)<1$ encoding local spectral bounds for a spin system, we derive global spectral-gap bounds for block dynamics on its marginal distributions. These bounds are sharp: the Gaussian system with covariance $(I-A)^{-1}$ attains equality for every choice of disjoint blocks. Our proof extends the Bochner method through an abstract inequality for orthogonal projections on Hilbert spaces. As an application, we prove that Glauber dynamics for the $O(N)$ model, with $N\geq 2$, arbitrary external fields, and couplings of either sign, has spectral gap at least $(1-\|J_{\mathrm{abs}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}/N)/n$, where $J$ is the interaction matrix and $J_{\mathrm{abs}}=(|J_{ij}|)$. We also obtain spectral bounds for swap walks and local spectral expansion of partite simplicial complexes. For complexes formed from disjoint groups of ranks in random flags of subspaces over $\mathbb F_q$, we obtain a one-sided local spectral expansion bound of $2\sqrt q/(q+1)$. This bound is independent of the number and sizes of each group, and is nontrivial for every prime power $q$. Finally, for random forests $F$ of any finite graph with arbitrary positive edge weights, we prove that \[ \Pr(e,f\in F)\le \frac{4}{3} \Pr(e\in F)\Pr(f\in F) \] for distinct edges $e,f$, improving the factor 2 supplied by general log-concavity bounds for matroid independent sets. The argument combines our extended Bochner method with the analysis of an auxiliary real stable polynomial.

papers.title: Logarithmic Regret for Alternating Mirror Descent
papers.abstract: Alternating online mirror descent (AltOMD) is a simple learning rule for zero-sum games, which improves upon simultaneous OMD numerically and theoretically. Previous work obtained $O(T^{1/3})$ and $O(T^{1/5})$ regret bounds for AltOMD, by leveraging modified-energy-function-based analyses. However, settling whether AltOMD achieves near-constant regret has remained an open question. In this paper we resolve the question of whether AltOMD achieves near-constant regret in the affirmative. In particular, we show an $O(log(T))$ regret bound on the sum of the players' external regrets for any two-player zero-sum bilinear game with compact convex strategy sets, under mild regularity assumptions on the regularizers. We verify that our assumptions hold for the negative entropy regularizer, thereby obtaining logarithmic regret for the alternating multiplicative weights updates algorithm. The regret bound also yields an $O(log(T)/T)$ duality gap bound for the averaged strategies.

papers.title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
papers.abstract: We attempt to alleviate failure modes of classical physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in scenarios of topological pathologies corresponding to punctures, holes, poles, and voids by introducing de Rham cohomological augmentations, or Hodge-de Rham PINNs. Vanilla PINNs often encounter pitfalls in hole-based settings due to discontinuous interfaces, nonzero closed path integration, path dependence, correspondence to exact forms via the exterior derivative, etc., therefore we absolve traditional failures via parameterizing a 1-form by the Hodge-Morrey-Friedrichs (HMF) decomposition for manifolds with boundary, drawing a connection to de Rham cohomology such as through the HMF isomorphism theorem. 1-forms can act as representations of scalar-valued PDE solutions through integral operator mappings. We propose performing a PINN-based loss on the parameterized 1-form through an associated PDE, which subsequently solves the potential-based PINN problem and moreover remedies the failures of vanilla PINNs via the Sobolev-regular operator under a Fréchet differentiation interconnection. The operator relationship often has a nontrivial closed-form and often requires integration or a case-by-case analysis, which we address thoroughly in our experiments. When an integrability condition is not met on our losses, we can equip exhaustion functions to train the networks. We demonstrate our methods on the Aharonov-Bohm effect, which, to our understanding, is largely nonexistent in PINN literature. We develop theoretical guarantees of our methods and demonstrate our pathological safeguards on a broad selection of topologically-adverse problems, including scenarios of inexact forms, and those of nontrivial harmonics and coexact terms.

papers.title: Minimal model of a Plateau-Rayleigh instability of a solid binary alloy nanowire: impacts of surface segregation
papers.abstract: Minimal model and its linear stability analysis (LSA) for Plateau-Rayleigh (PR) instability of an intermixed, solid binary alloy nanowire is presented. Model accounts only for the surface diffusions of the alloy components without anisotropies of a surface energies, and for a classical thermodynamic surface segregation. Model allows to assess a deviation of a longwave instability cutoff wavelength $λ_c$ from the classical value $2πr_0$ (a wire circumference) as a function of a surface composition deviation from its equilibrium value, a wire radius, and a bulk concentration of a minority component. Results of LSA are presented for AuNi, PtNi, and CoNi nanowires, where an important distinction is that a surface segregation curve for CoNi is qualitatively different from the one for AuNi and PtNi. For each nanowire there is a sizable region of a parameter space where $λ_c<2πr_0$ and correspondingly, a fastest growing perturbation wavelength $λ_{max}$ is also less than a wire circumference. This is in stark contrast to PR instability of a single-component nanowire transporting mass by surface diffusion - in this case $λ_c$ and $λ_{max}$ are larger than a wire circumference. Strong surface segregation is primarily responsible for unusually small $λ_c$ and $λ_{max}$. Results suggest that a large number of small and closely spaced nanoparticles may emerge upon disintegration via annealing of a binary alloy nanowire.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Happy Edge Conjecture in Plane Spanning Trees
papers.abstract: We study the problem of reconfiguring plane, straight-line spanning trees on point sets in the plane. A flip is a reconfiguration step in which one edge of a tree is replaced with another, yielding again a plane spanning tree. For a given point set $P$, the flip graph has a vertex for each plane spanning tree on $P$, and an edge between any two trees that differ by a single flip. The folklore happy edge conjecture suggests that any edge shared by both the initial and the target tree (a happy edge) is never flipped in a shortest flip sequence. This conjecture was computationally verified for up to 10 points in convex position. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture both on general point sets and on point sets in convex position by providing two counterexamples on $16$ and $30$ points, respectively. The counterexample for point sets in general position also holds for compatible flips, while the happy edge property holds for compatible flips in convex point sets as shown by Aichholzer, Dorfer, and Vogtenhuber [GD 2025].

papers.title: An Exact QFT/Lattice Map for Fermions
papers.abstract: We construct an exact map between continuum fermion fields and lattice fields in 1+1 dimensions. This map rewrites a continuum Hamiltonian as a lattice Hamiltonian with nearest-neighbor couplings and an infinite-dimensional local Hilbert space. The resulting lattice model reproduces exactly the energy spectrum, global operator algebra, chiral symmetries, and anomalies of the continuum QFT on any finite lattice. Unlike domain wall fermions, truncating the local Hilbert space introduces no extra massless modes, and the entanglement entropy of an interval converges as the truncation is removed. The lattice local algebras are of type I and lie between the type III continuum algebras of nested spatial regions, in accordance with the split property. We demonstrate this construction explicitly for $N$ Majorana fermions, realizing the $\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{L}\times\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{R}$ lattice chiral symmetry. We also construct an exact lattice model for the Schwinger model and numerically reproduce the mass gap $e/\sqrtπ$.

papers.title: Boundary $c\leq1$ Liouville CFT from the Bootstrap
papers.abstract: We construct boundary Liouville conformal field theory at central charge $c\leq1$ with FZZT-type boundary conditions and show that it satisfies the Cardy--Lewellen sewing constraints on the disk and the annulus. Using the analytic bootstrap we derive the so far missing boundary three-point and bulk-to-boundary structure constants and a consistent disk one-point function as explicit meromorphic functions of the Liouville momenta. In sharp contrast to $c\geq25$, the open-string spectrum between two ``timelike'' FZZT boundaries is \emph{discrete}, yet non-trivially consistent through open-closed duality with the \emph{continuous} closed-string spectrum of Ribault and Santachiara.

papers.title: O-segments on topological measure spaces
papers.abstract: Let $μ$ be a finite non-atomic measure on a set $X$. A \emph{segment} for $μ$ is an increasing family $u(t)$, $t\in[0,1]$, of measurable sets with $u(0)=\emptyset$, $u(1)=X$ and $μ(u(t))=t\,μ(X)$; by a theorem of Fryszkowski, finitely many measures $f\,dμ$ admit a common segment. We study \emph{open segments}, i.e.\ segments consisting of open sets, when $X$ carries a topology. We show that weak outer regularity of $μ$ is equivalent to the approximability of measurable sets by open sets, and that it holds for every finite Borel measure on a metrizable space. Our main result states that if $μ$ is finite, non-atomic and weakly outer regular, then for all $f,g\in L^1(μ)$ with $(\int f\,dμ,\int g\,dμ)\neq(0,0)$ there is a common open segment for $f\,dμ$ and $g\,dμ$; in particular, for every $f\in L^1(μ)$ there is an open segment for $μ$ which is simultaneously a segment for $f\,dμ$. Relative versions allow one to prescribe an initial set. We also characterize open segments as upper semicontinuous functions with uniform distribution and show that on separable metrizable spaces a single measure admits such a function which is continuous.

papers.title: On a property of plane curves
papers.abstract: Let $γ:[0,1]\to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a continuous curve with $γ(0)=(0,0)$ and $γ(1)=(1,1)$. We prove that if $γ(t)\in(0,1)^2$ for all $t\in(0,1)$, then for each $n\in \mathbb{N}$ there exist points $A_1,\dots,A_n$ on $γ$ such that, with $A_0=(0,0)$ and $A_{n+1}=(1,1)$, the horizontal increments $π_1(\overrightarrow{A_iA_{i+1}})$ and the vertical increments $π_2(\overrightarrow{A_iA_{i+1}})$, $0\le i\le n$, are positive and coincide up to order. More generally, the same conclusion holds as soon as $γ$ contains an arc that joins two points of the diagonal segment, lies on one side of the diagonal, and satisfies a mild one-sided boundary condition. This covers, for instance, the graph of every continuous function $f$ with $f(0)=0$ and $f(1)=1$, with no restriction on the range of $f$. In all cases the rearrangement can be taken to be a cyclic shift by one place of a block of consecutive increments. The main tool is a version of the mountain climbers' theorem in which one function is piecewise monotone and the other is an arbitrary continuous function. As an application, any two non-atomic probability measures on $[0,1]$ satisfying a mild condition admit, for each $n$, a partition of $[0,1]$ into $n+1$ consecutive intervals whose two lists of measures are rearrangements of each other.
papers.comments: This is a revised version of a published article
papers.journal_ref: M. Javaheri, On a property of plane curves, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 361 (2010), 332--337

papers.title: Magnetism and infrared divergence in a Hubbard-phonon interacting system
papers.abstract: We study a finite Hubbard model coupled to a massless phonon field through a form factor common to all sites that satisfies the infrared singular condition. The Hamiltonian has no ground state in the Fock representation. With the unitary transformation of Arai and Hirokawa, the ground states with infrared cutoff define states on the Weyl algebra over the form domain of the inverse dispersion, and they converge to a ground state in a representation inequivalent to the Fock representation. In this representation the ground states are the products of the ground states of the Hubbard model and the phonon vacuum, so that the model has ferromagnetic or unique spin-singlet ground states according to the hopping matrix and the electron number.

papers.title: Phonon Bose-Einstein condensation in a Hubbard-phonon interacting system with infrared divergence
papers.abstract: We study the grand canonical Gibbs states of a finite Hubbard model coupled to massless phonons with the dispersion relation $|k|^s$, $1\leq s<d$, at finite temperature. We keep the decoupling setting of the zero-temperature analysis, in which the electron-phonon form factor is common to all sites. An explicit unitary transformation factorizes the Gibbs state into the electron Gibbs state and the free phonon Gibbs state up to a phase, and the phonons exhibit Bose-Einstein condensation in the thermodynamic limit with the critical density of the free Bose gas. Assuming the convergence of this phase as the infrared cutoff is removed, the condensed state is the mixture of mutually disjoint component states with broken gauge symmetry, described by their expectations on the Weyl algebra. Physically, phonons are considered not to undergo Bose-Einstein condensation arxiv:1207.4621, and the study of a mechanism that suppresses this mathematical and formal condensation is left for future research.

papers.title: Drinfeld J Presentation of Twisted Yangians
papers.abstract: We present a quantization of a Lie coideal structure for twisted half-loop algebras of finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebras. We obtain algebra closure relations of twisted Yangians in Drinfeld J presentation for all symmetric pairs of simple Lie algebras and for simple twisted even half-loop Lie algebras. We provide the explicit form of the closure relations for twisted Yangians in Drinfeld J presentation for the ${\mathfrak{sl}}_3$ Lie algebra.
papers.comments: v4: Corrected and completed coefficient tensors in (5.14) and (5.21)

papers.title: Sharp Poincaré inequalities for the logarithmic smoothness of the Gauss map on hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We establish sharp lower bounds for two geometric functionals which evaluate the global variation of the Gauss map on the boundary of bounded open sets $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. These functionals arise as the endpoint case $s=0$ of the Gagliardo seminorm in $W^{s,p}(\partialΩ)$ of the normal vector field, for $p\in\{1,2\}$. We also show that balls are the unique minimizers. In addition, some applications to the fractional setting $s>0$ are given.
papers.comments: 28 pages. The title has been modified, and new sections covering motivation and applications have been added. The results have been strengthened compared to previous versions

papers.title: Parametrized Euler class and semicohomology theory
papers.abstract: Given a measurable cocycle with values in $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\mathbb{S}^1)$, we construct an $\mathrm{L}^\infty$-parametrized Euler class in bounded cohomology. We show that such a class vanishes if and only if the cocycle can be lifted to $\mathrm{Homeo}^+_{\mathbb{Z}}(\mathbb{R})$ and it admits an equivariant family of points. We recall the notion of semicohomologous cocycles and we show that two measurable cocycles are semicohomologous if and only if they induce the same parametrized Euler class. Since for minimal cocycles, semicohomology boils down to cohomology, the parametrized Euler classes of minimal cohomologous cocycles are equal. We conclude by studying the vanishing of the real parametrized Euler class and we obtain some results about elementary cocycles.
papers.comments: 30 pages, improved exposition, to appear on BBMS

papers.title: Hilbert's 16th problem through Morse theory
papers.abstract: We focus on the second part of Hilbert's 16th problem and provide an upper bound on the number of limit cycles that a polynomial, differential, planar system may have, depending exclusively on the degree $n$ of the system. Such a bound turns out to be a polynomial of degree $4$ in $n$. More specifically, if $H(n)$ indicates the maximum number of limit cycles among planar, differential, polynomial systems of degree $n$, then \begin{gather} H(n)\le \dfrac52 n^4-\dfrac{23}2 n^3+ \dfrac{43}2n^2-\dfrac{37}2n+7\,\,\,\, \mbox{if $n$ is even, and} \nonumber H(n)\le \dfrac52 n^4-\dfrac{23}2 n^3+ \dfrac{41}2n^2-\dfrac{33}2n+6\,\,\,\, \mbox{if $n$ is odd}.\nonumber \end{gather} For quadratic systems, we find $H(2)=4$. Our proof is entirely variational and utilizes in a fundamental way tools and facts from Morse theory, to the point that no particular expertise in dynamical systems is necessary or required. It is particularly interesting to compare our results with the ones for the same problem recently announced and made public by OpenAI as part of the solution of hundreds of important mathematical problems.

papers.title: A Note On Majorizing Norms on Majorized Spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce a new type of norm for ordered vector spaces majorized by a proper (convex) cone that generalizes the notions of order unit norm and base norm. Then we give sufficient conditions to ensure its completeness. In the case of normed Riesz spaces, we also present necessary completeness conditions and describe the completed norm. Finally, we define a particular family of well-behaving sets. Spaces majorized by the cone generated by these sets display surprisingly interesting structural properties. In particular, we generalize two famous standard results in Banach lattice theory. Namely, every principal ideal in a Banach lattice is an AM-space and every Banach lattice having a generating cone with a compact base admits an equivalent L-norm.
papers.comments: 13 pages. v3 corrects several false statements of v2 (Lemma 14, Theorem 21, Corollaries 16, 22, 26, 37, 38, Example 5, Proposition 30): Theorem 21 is refuted by an explicit counterexample in c_0, Theorem 18 now has a direct proof, and the statements about coherent sets are revised accordingly. "`

papers.title: Harmonic analysis approach to the relative Riemann-Roch theorem on global fields
papers.abstract: In this paper we generalize and put in a new light part of ``Fouier analysis on Number fields and Hecke's zeta function''[14] by Tate. We express the relative Euler characteristic using purely adelic language. By using certain natural normalization of Haar measure on adeles we obtain the relative Riemann-Roch theorem. In particular we show that using our relative normalization of the Haar measure on adeles we can obtain the relative Riemann-Roch theorem from the adelic Poisson summation formulae. In addition, using our methods we define the relative 'size of cohomology' numbers, i.e. extract the $h^0$ and $h^1$ part of the relative Euler characteristic. Our theory not only covers both absolute and relative cases, but also the case of an arithmetic curve and a nonsingular, projective curve over a finite field.
papers.comments: 15 pages, corrections and adding new results

papers.title: The Collatz Conjecture & Non-Archimedean Spectral Theory -- Part II -- $\left(p,q\right)$-Adic Fourier Analysis and Wiener's Tauberian Theorem
papers.abstract: This paper gives an overview of $\left(p,q\right)$-adic Fourier theory - the Fourier theory of functions from the $p$-adic numbers to the $q$-adic numbers, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes - which we then use to prove a novel $\left(p,q\right)$-adic generalization of Norbert Wiener's celebrated Tauberian Theorem. Letting $K$ be a metrically complete, algebraically closed local field of residue characteristic $q$, letting $C\left(\mathbb{Z}_{p},K\right)$ be the Banach space of continuous functions $\mathbb{Z}_{p}\rightarrow K$, and letting $dμ$ be a $\left(p,q\right)$-adic measure (a continuous linear functional $C\left(\mathbb{Z}_{p},K\right)\rightarrow K)$, the $\left(p,q\right)$-adic Wiener Tauberian Theorem (WTT) we prove establishes that the density of the span of translates of $dμ$'s Fourier-Stieltjes Transform implies the non-vanishing of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of $dμ$ at all points in $\mathbb{Z}_{p}$ where the derivative exists in $K$.

papers.title: $P=W$ via $\mathcal{H}_2$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}_2$ be the Lie algebra of polynomial Hamiltonian vector fields on the symplectic plane. Let $X$ be the moduli space of stable Higgs bundles of fixed relatively prime rank and degree, or more generally the moduli space of stable parabolic Higgs bundles of arbitrary rank and degree for a generic stability condition. Let $H^*(X)$ be the cohomology with rational coefficients. Using the operations of cup-product by tautological classes and Hecke correspondences we construct an action of $\mathcal{H}_2$ on $H^*(X)[x,y]$, where $x$ and $y$ are formal variables. We show that the perverse filtration on $H^*(X)$ coincides with the filtration canonically associated to $\mathfrak{sl}_2\subset \mathcal{H}_2$ and deduce the $P=W$ conjecture of de Cataldo-Hausel-Migliorini.
papers.comments: v3: 56 pages. Final version, expanded introduction. v2: 54 pages. Improved exposition, added many details, W-algebra setup split into arXiv:2311.13415

papers.title: Homology with the theme of Matlis
papers.abstract: Matlis proved a lot of homological properties of the fraction field of an integral domain. In this paper, we simplify and extend some of them from 1-dimensional (resp. rank one) cases to the higher dimensional (resp. finite rank) cases. For example, we study the weakly co-torsion property of Ext$(-,\sim)$, and use it to present splitting criteria. These are equipped with several applications. For instance, we compute the projective dimension of $\widehat{R}$ and present some non-noetherian versions of Grothendieck's localization problem. We construct a new class of co-Hopfian modules and extend Matlis' decomposability problem to higher ranks. In particular, this paper deals with the basic properties of Matlis' quadric $(Q,Q/R, \widehat{R},\overset{\sim}R).$

papers.title: Biexact von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of biexactness for general von Neumann algebras, naturally extending the notion from group theory. We show that biexactness implies solidity for von Neumann algebras, and that many of the examples of solid von Neumann algebras contained in the literature are, in fact, biexact. We also give examples of certain crossed products arising from Gaussian actions that are solid but not biexact, and we give examples of certain $q$-Gaussian von Neumann algebras that are strongly solid but not biexact. The techniques developed involve studying a certain weak form of nuclear embeddings, and we use this setting to give a new description of weak exactness for von Neumann algebras, which allows us to answer several open problems in the literature about weakly exact von Neumann algebras.

papers.title: Connected Dominating Sets in Triangulations
papers.abstract: A dominating set of a graph $G$ is \emph{connected} if it induces a connected graph in $G$. For planar triangulations, it has been known since 1990 that every $n$-vertex triangulation with $n\ge4$ admits a connected dominating set of size at most $n/2 - 1$, and no improvement to this bound was known for over three decades. We break this longstanding barrier by showing that every $n$-vertex triangulation has a connected dominating set of size at most $10n/21$. Equivalently, every triangulation admits a spanning tree with at least $11n/21$ leaves. This result has graph drawing applications, establishing a bound for one-bend free sets and improving the known bound for simultaneous planar embeddings. The connected dominating set results extend readily to show that an $n$-vertex triangulation of a surface of Euler genus $g$ has a connected dominating set of size at most $10n/21+O(\sqrt{gn})$.
papers.comments: Updated version with several corrections and improvements. Most notably, the use of potential functions rather than linear programs to bound the sizes of dominating sets

papers.title: Fundamental groups, coregularity, and low dimensional klt Calabi-Yau pairs
papers.abstract: In this article, we study how the absolute coregularity of a projective log pair reflects on its fundamental group. More precisely, we conjecture that for a projective klt log pair $(X,D)$ of absolute coregularity $c$ (and arbitrary dimension) the fundamental group $π_1^{\rm reg}(X,D)$ admits a normal abelian subgroup of finite index and rank at most $2c$. We prove this conjecture in the cases $0 \leq c \leq 3$, building on the almost abelianity of the fundamental groups of klt Calabi-Yau pairs of dimension $\leq 3$. In the cases $c \in \{0,1,2\}$ and fixed dimension, we can furthermore bound the index of a solvable normal subgroup. In dimension three, we are able to prove almost abelianity of the fundamental group of the regular locus for projective klt Calabi-Yau pairs.
papers.comments: This paper is superseded by arXiv:2610.21358 with substantial corrections and improvements, in particular we prove therein in all dimensions the virtual abelianity of orbifold fundamental groups of the smooth loci of projective klt pairs with trivial and nef log anticanonical divisor

papers.title: Upper estimates of the lifespan for the fractional wave equations with time-dependent damping and a power nonlinearity of subcritical and critical Fujita exponent
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Cauchy problem of the fractional wave equation with time-dependent damping and the source nonlinearity $f(u)\approx |u|^p$: $$ \begin{cases} \partial_t^2u(t,x)+(-Δ)^{σ/2} u(t,x)+b(t) \partial_t u(t,x) =f(u(t,x)),\ &(t,x)\ \in [0,T)\times \mathbb{R}^N,\\ u(0,x)=u_0(x),\ \partial_tu(0,x)=u_1(x),\ &x\ \in\ \mathbb{R}^N, \end{cases} $$ where the damping coefficient behaves as $b(t)\approx (1+t)^{-β}$. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of mild and strong solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces by deriving weighted Sobolev estimates for the linear propagators and overcoming the spatial-weight coupling in the nonlinearity through the Bessel potential estimates. Then, in the subcritical and critical cases $1<p\leq p_c:=1+\frac σN$, we derive the upper estimates of the lifespan for the fractional Laplacian with $0<σ<2$ and time-dependent damping $β\in [-1, 1)$ via the framework of ordinary differential inequalities.
