We discuss consequences for the center of cyclotomic Hecke algebras and for specializations to q=1 and to roots of unity. In particular, we relate K-theory of affine type A quiver varieties with the centers of the corresponding blocks of specialized cyclotomic Hecke algebras. This last result strengthens the correspondences obtained by the second author in earlier work.

papers.title: Quantitative Soft-to-Hard Terminal Constraint Convergence for the Heat Equation
papers.abstract: We investigate an optimal control problem for the one-dimensional heat equation with a prescribed terminal state. To approximate the hard terminal constraint, we consider quadratic terminal penalization and analyze the convergence of the optimal controls and terminal states as the penalty parameter \(α\to\infty\). We develop a unified spectral treatment of terminal reachability, minimum-energy control, and quadratic-penalty convergence. Using modal decompositions, we characterize finite-energy admissible terminal targets and construct the corresponding minimum-energy hard-constrained control. For admissible targets, we establish strong convergence of penalized optimal controls and terminal states. Under suitable spectral summability conditions, we obtain regularity-dependent convergence estimates of order \(O(α^{-(1/2+θ)})\) for the terminal-state error, \(0\leθ\le1/2\), and \(O(α^{-θ})\) for the optimal-control error, \(0<θ\le1\). The analysis connects these results explicitly with classical Tikhonov regularization in the heat-equation setting. A finite-dimensional prototype illustrates the underlying projection structure, while companion numerical investigations provide supporting evidence for the predicted convergence behavior.
papers.comments: 30 pages; revised introduction, references, and discussion of Tikhonov regularization

papers.title: Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex, which can be considered as a derived variant of the module of Frobenius--Witt differentials defined by T. Saito. This new object also can be seen as an arithmetic variant of the notion of cotangent complex. We explain the suitability of these two viewpoints through a series of propositions. Furthermore, we establish a relationship between Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes and the regularity of noetherian local rings, which can be considered as a derived variant of Saito's regularity criterion. This proof relies heavily on computations of Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes in the case of perfectoid rings. We also study the deformation theory of delta structures using Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes.
papers.comments: 30 pages. Comments are very welcome. v4: corrected the proof of Theorem 5.9. v3: added an application to the deformation theory of delta structures and corrected typos. v2: minor corrections and a generalization of one of the main theorems

papers.title: Notes on obstructions in the hyperbolic Clifford algebra bundle structure
papers.abstract: Starting from a general analysis of obstruction classes, we develop the investigation of obstructions associated with the bundle structure of the hyperbolic Clifford algebra. By taking into account particularities arising from the Whitney sum, it is shown that, unlike classical tangent bundle cases, the hyperbolic frame bundle of an oriented manifold admits lifting without any topological obstruction, that is, it admits a structure of the connected double covering of $\mathrm{GL}^{+}(2m,\mathbb{R})$, and the hyperbolic tangent bundle carries a $Spin^{e}_{m,m}$ structure (with $m=\dim\mathcal{M}$), whatever the value of $w_2(\mathcal{M})$. These conclusions are known from the work of Karoubi and Gualtieri and the point of this note is that they follow from the Whitney product formula alone, or from the additivity formula of Whitney sums with an explicit covering group, without recourse to Karoubi's criterion for indefinite signature. We also describe the spinor bundles involved, which are bundles of differential forms and not Dirac spinor bundles and show that orientability is needed for the covering of the full linear group.

papers.title: On the geodesic midrange crossing constant
papers.abstract: We introduce an analytic framework for studying the number of crossings in planar straight-line and spherical geodesic drawings; we begin by analyzing drawings in a continuous setting and then pass to finite graphs. We use this approach to derive multiple results. First, we show that the midrange crossing constant is strictly smaller than $8/(9π^2)$, improving the best known upper bound of Pach and Tóth from nearly thirty years ago. Second, we prove sharp lower bounds for some restricted drawing classes. For spherical geodesic drawings with uniformly distributed vertices, we determine the minimum number of crossings at every edge density. We also prove lower bounds for planar straight line drawings in compact convex domains with uniform vertex sets. Consequently, we determine the restricted midrange crossing constant to be $8/(9π^2)$ in both of these settings. Finally, for two-layer bipartite drawings, with straight edges between two parallel lines, we determine the midrange crossing constant to be $2/3$.
papers.comments: 28 pages, 4 figures. It now includes the counter-example and lower bound for two-layer bipartite drawings

papers.title: Adams filtrations and secondary coherence for fibers of Steenrod operations
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Bruner--Rognes two-extension theorem and open questions regarding the secondary cohomology modeling of fibers of Steenrod operations, we develop a general framework to compute their Adams filtrations and delineate the underlying algebraic obstructions. Let $f:Y\to\prodΣ^{d_λ}H\mathbb F_2$ be a locally finite family of positive-degree stable operations, where $Y=H\mathbb F_2$ or $H\mathbb Z$. We determine the Adams filtration of its fiber from the minimal generators of $\operatorname{im}(f^*)$ as a left Steenrod module. An explicit target automorphism separates a minimal subfamily, and combining this with the two-extension theorem and an acyclic cancellation gives $E_3=E_\infty$. A terminating Adem recursion realizes this splitting for the full positive even-square family. Separately, we identify two fundamental algebraic obstructions to directly constructing the secondary cohomology of these fibers: an augmentation discrepancy when the primary row has a nonzero kernel, and a coherence obstruction class in the third cohomology of a Hom complex. These results demonstrate why the secondary Ext groups of these fibers must be derived topologically via the Baues--Jibladze comparison theorem, rather than through a direct algebraic resolution.
papers.comments: 21 pages. This new version supersedes v2 and withdraws its unsupported claims to resolve Bruner's Questions 6.1 and 6.2. Instead, it rigorously delineates the structural obstructions that make a direct algebraic secondary modeling of these fibers impossible

papers.title: Halász theorems for Gaussian ideals in sectors and short intervals
papers.abstract: We prove a quantitative Halász theorem for multiplicative functions on the nonzero ideals of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, with bounds controlled by pretentious distance to the Archimedean characters $N^{it}$. We also prove a sectorial analogue: under angular non-pretentiousness, the sum of $f$ over ideals lying in a fixed sector is asymptotically given by the expected proportion of the unrestricted sum. Finally, under angular non-pretentiousness and a non-degeneracy condition on conjugate prime pairs, we prove a sectorial short-interval version of the Halász theorem for annular sectors whose radial thickness tends to infinity. The proof of the sectorial short-interval Halász theorem uses angular Fourier expansion, norm-compression to multiplicative functions on $\mathbb{N}$, and a theorem of Mangerel.

papers.title: On the Hodge and Tate conjectures for moduli spaces of curves
papers.abstract: We survey recent progress on the cohomology of moduli spaces of stable curves through the lens of the Hodge and Tate conjectures, especially their generalized coniveau forms, which relate Hodge structures and l-adic Galois representations on cohomology to algebraic cycles. We explain how the inductive structure of the boundary stratification verifies these conjectures in a surprisingly wide range of cases, describe the guiding inspiration from arithmetic, and discuss open problems and directions for future research.
papers.comments: v2: 28 pages, minor revisions and expository improvements. Final version to appear in the proceedings of the 2025 Summer Research Institute in Algebraic Geometry

papers.title: Boundary Blowup Solutions for the Finsler p-Laplacian: Wellposedness and Asymptotic Behaviour
papers.abstract: We study the existence of large (boundary blow-up) solutions to semilinear equations involving the Finsler p-Laplacian on bounded domains with sufficiently smooth boundaries. We establish a Keller-Osserman-type condition that ensures the existence of such solutions, and show that this condition retains the same integrability as that of the p-Laplacian. We examine the influence of the anisotropic norm underlying the Finsler p-Laplacian on the boundary behaviour of the solution, then derive asymptotic estimates for large solutions near the boundary of the domain. Using these boundary asymptotics, we prove uniqueness results for power-type nonlinearities.
papers.comments: Some changes in the comparison principle and the local bound of the solutions. The existence of a large radial solution on a ball is added

papers.title: On higher order Morrey's inequalities over CD{\boldmath$(K,N)$}-spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a higher order Morrey's inequality in the framework of $\mathsf{CD}(K,N)$-spaces for $K\in\mathbb{R}$ and $N\in\mathbb{N}$. We do so by first introducing an alternate version of second order Sobolev spaces in general metric measure spaces, which contains amply many functions even when $p>N$. These spaces contain the traditional $H^{2, p}(X)$ spaces on $\mathsf{RCD}(K, N)$-spaces.
papers.comments: 33 pages, some results are now valid in the setting of CD spaces, title change. Comments welcome!

papers.title: On Zappa-Szép products of two semidihedral groups
papers.abstract: Let $n, m \ge 4$. We study the Zappa--Szép products $G = HK$ with $H = \langle x\rangle \rtimes \langle y\rangle \cong SD_{2^n}$ and $K = \langle z\rangle \rtimes \langle w\rangle \cong SD_{2^m}$, together with the fixed generators $x, y, z, w$, and we describe the parameter tuples which encode the mixed commutators of these generators, according to the cores of $\langle x\rangle$ and $\langle z\rangle$ in~$G$. First, when both $\langle x\rangle$ and $\langle z\rangle$ are normal in~$G$, we show that the admissible parameter tuples are exactly the solutions of an explicit system of six polynomial congruences. Second, when the cores $\langle x\rangle_G$ and $\langle z\rangle_G$ are arbitrary subgroups of $\langle x\rangle$ and $\langle z\rangle$, under the simplifying assumption $[x, z] = 1$, and for generating systems for which all mixed commutators lie in $\langle x\rangle\langle z\rangle$, we obtain an analogous classification by twelve congruences together with two order conditions; this is the semidihedral counterpart of the Hu--Yu classification~\cite{HuYu2025} for dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ and $D_{2m}$ with $n, m$ odd. In contrast with that case, we further construct an explicit exact product with both cores non-trivial and $[x, z] \ne 1$, so that the semidihedral setting contains additional families of exact products.

papers.title: Thermalization with Gaussian Quantum Cellular Automata
papers.abstract: We study the long-time dynamics of many-body bosonic lattice systems under translation-invariant Gaussian quantum cellular automata. We formulate two sets of conditions on GQCAs which separately guarantee thermalization of any state on the local Weyl algebra to the infinite temperature state, whenever the state is locally normal and has uniformly bounded particle density. Our main intermediate result is a quantum many-body generalization of the classic Riemann-Lebesgue lemma which is a bound on expectation values of local Weyl operators involving their support and the state's particle density.
papers.comments: 24 pages, 1 figure, v2 is a minor revision

papers.title: Generating functions and efficient numerical simulation of aggregation-fragmentation kinetics
papers.abstract: In this work, we review and revisit the generating function techniques that provide exact analytical solutions for aggregation and fragmentation equations across several physical regimes including spontaneous and collisional shattering. For discrete coagulation-fragmentation equations with size-independent rates under monodisperse initial conditions, we show the derivation of several explicit closed-form solutions. We also briefly report the exact solutions for continuous, three-particle, $D$-particle collisions and two-component generalizations. Source-driven aggregation yields steady distributions featuring a universal $s^{-3/2}$ power-law decay and a cutoff mass scaling $s_{*} \sim t^{2}$. We also remind that exploitation of the low-rank representations of the aggregation kernel allows to organize efficient modelling the aggregation kinetics and extend this idea showing a simple way for the fast accounting of the spontaneous framentation terms. We exploit our numerical algorithm and study the numerical solutions for multiple models of spontaneous fragmentation and find a new example of temporal oscillations for the closed aggregation-fragmentation process.

papers.title: Spreading speeds for prey-predator systems in a shifting environment: a short proof
papers.abstract: This note is concerned with the spreading speed of the predator component in a class of prey-predator reaction-diffusion systems with spatiotemporal heterogeneity depending on a moving variable. The main difficulty is that the full system lacks a direct comparison principle. We establish a pointwise estimate showing that the prey density is close to its carrying capacity wherever the predator density is sufficiently small. This allows us to compare solutions of the system with those of scalar Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments. Consequently, we obtain an explicit formula for the spreading speed of the predator. In particular, for nonmonotone shifting environments, locking and nonlocal pulling phenomena may occur.

papers.title: Spreading speeds for nonlocal Fisher-KPP equations with time-dependent asymmetric kernels
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish spreading speeds for a nonlocal Fisher-KPP equation with measurable time-dependent asymmetric kernels, without imposing an inequality between growth and diffusion or requiring the kernel to be positive near the origin. The kernel has a time independent upper bound which is thin-tailed. Both the kernel and the linear growth rate have uniform means. Under these assumptions, we determine the exact rightward and leftward spreading speeds and prove convergence to the positive equilibrium inside the spreading interval. The proof is based on comparison arguments and a family of compactly supported subsolutions. Explicit examples show that time-dependent dispersal kernels with the same time average can exhibit different propagation behaviors.

papers.title: Decoupled energy-stable Runge-Kutta schemes of arbitrary order for the anisotropic phase-field dendritic crystal growth model
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel and general framework for constructing arbitrary-order, energy-stable, and decoupled schemes for the anisotropic phase-field dendritic crystal growth model. The proposed framework combines a time-dependent auxiliary variable, an algebraically stable Runge-Kutta method, and a matrix diagonalization technique. This unique combination yields a scheme that is proven to be unconditionally energy-dissipative while requiring only the solution of independent, constant-coefficient elliptic equations at each time step, which can be solved in parallel. The auxiliary variable is recovered from a uniquely solvable $q\times q$ algebraic system. We provide a rigorous proof of $q$th-order convergence in time for a $q$-stage Runge-Kutta method within a fixed Fourier-Galerkin space. Numerical experiments in 2D and 3D not only confirm the theoretical convergence and energy stability but also demonstrate the efficiency of the decoupled approach and provide a detailed investigation of key parameters' effects on dendritic morphology.

papers.title: Integrality of height-one formal groups
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove that a one-dimensional formal group law over $K$ has integral coefficients if and only if its multiplication-by-$n$ endomorphisms have integral coefficients for all integers $n$, in the height-one case, that is when the multiplication by $p$ has Weierstrass degree $p$. The proof relies on $p$-adic Hodge theory.

papers.title: A $Tb$ type theorem for suppressed kernels
papers.abstract: In this article, a non-homogeneous $Tb$ type theorem for arbitrary dimensional Calderón-Zygmund singular integral operators is proved. This is an extension of an analogous non-homogeneous $Tb$ theorem for the Cauchy transform, in the planar setting, due to Nazarov, Treil and Volberg. The novelties of the present work are the change of dimension and the fact that the operators to which the theorem applies are not necessarily antisymmetric. The techniques used in the proof include, among others, suppressed kernels, decompositions in $L^2(μ)$, where $μ$ is a Radon measure in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and a probabilistic argument resulting from taking averages of the operators involved.

papers.title: Discrete homotopy groups of cubical sets
papers.abstract: We extend the notion of discrete homotopy groups of graphs to arbitrary cubical sets, and show that the discrete homotopy groups of quasisymmetric cubical sets are naturally isomorphic to the homotopy groups of their geometric realizations. Here, quasisymmetric cubical sets are cubical sets equipped with coordinate permutation symmetries that are compatible with faces and degeneracies, but not necessarily with connections. We give a purely combinatorial construction of the left adjoint of the forgetful functor from the category of quasisymmetric cubical sets to the category of cubical sets, and prove that the unit of this adjunction is a natural weak equivalence. As a consequence, we obtain a purely combinatorial description of the homotopy groups of the geometric realizations of arbitrary cubical sets. As an application, we establish the discrete Hurewicz map from the discrete homotopy groups of a cubical set to the homology groups, and prove a Hurewicz theorem with respect to the discrete Hurewicz map whenever the cubical set is quasisymmetric. Applied to the 1-nerve of a directed graph, it also yields a Hurewicz theorem relating the homotopy groups of Li, Wu, Yau, and Zhang to singular cubical homology.
papers.comments: We replace $\mathcal{G}_0\$ by $\mathrm{Ex}^{\infty}$ in the proofs of the comparison and Hurewicz theorems for quasisymmetric cubical sets. We revise the definition of $\mathcal{S}$, and also reformulate grids as cubical maps from geometric products of zigzags

papers.title: Cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-Homology from Bruhat Boundary Matrices of Split Semisimple Flag Varieties
papers.abstract: We determine the cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-chain complex of full and partial flag varieties of split semisimple simply connected groups over a perfect field of characteristic different from 2. With compatible integral normal orientations and reindexing by opposite Bruhat cells, the differential in each degree at least two is represented by the motivic Hopf map $η$ times one half of the signed cellular boundary matrix of the corresponding real flag manifold. Consequently, the Smith data of the resulting integer complex give all positive-degree cellular homology sheaves in terms of Milnor--Witt $K$-theory and the kernels and cokernels of integer multiples of $η$. We obtain a uniform computation of the second cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-homology of $SL_n/B$ for $n\geq3$, together with complete calculations for $SL_3/B$ and the full flags of types $F_4$ and $G_2$.

papers.title: The Exact Ville Identity with Applications to E-Values
papers.abstract: Let $M_n$ be a nonnegative supermartingale with $M_0=1$, and let $T_b$ be the first time $M_n$ crosses $b>1$. Ville's inequality gives $P(T_b<\infty)\leq 1/b$. We show that, at every finite time horizon $N$, $$ 1=bP(T_b\leq N)+V_{b,N}+D_{b,N}+R_{b,N}, $$ where $V_{b,N}$ is the expected overshoot at crossing, $D_{b,N}$ is the cumulative predictable decrease before crossing, and $R_{b,N}$ is the expected value of paths that up to the time horizon $N$ remained below the boundary $b$. The identity follows from telescoping and can be made horizon free without additional integrability assumption. It gives a formula for the slack in Ville's inequality and thus the conservatism of the threshold test $M_n\geq b$. For likelihood ratio martingales, the same terms also describe power: $R_{b,N}$ is the probability, under the alternative, of not crossing by $N$, whereas $bP(T_b\leq N)+V_{b,N}$ is the power. The identity also allows us to verify horizon-free guarantees from a finite computation: $P(T_b<\infty)$ lies between $P(T_b\leq N)$ and $P(T_b\leq N)+R_{b,N}/b$, so a proposed threshold test $M_n\geq b_α$ can be shown to be of level $α\in(0,1)$ for every time horizon based on computations at the single horizon $N$. We illustrate how Ville's identity yields sharper thresholds for Bernoulli and exponential likelihood-ratio tests, and for a conformal test of exchangeability, demonstrating Monte Carlo calibration under a composite, nonparametric null. Lastly, we also establish a continuous-time analogue of Ville's identity.

papers.title: A note on prismatic sites for p-quasisyntomic rings
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a fixed prime number and let $R$ be a $p$-quasisyntomic ring. We provide conditions for objects in the absolute prismatic site $R_\Prism$ to cover the final object in $\Shv(R_\Prism)$ and to admit finite self-coproducts in $R_\Prism$. More precisely, we introduce in $R_\Prism$ the so-called transversal objects, so that the coproduct of any object in $R_\Prism$ with a transversal object exists in $R_\Prism$. As an immediate generalization, we introduce the so-called relatively quasiregular semiperfectoid covers of $R$, whose prismatic cohomology (of $δ$-pairs, in the sense of Antieau-Krause-Nikolaus) produces objects in $R_\Prism$ that cover the final object in $\Shv(R_\Prism)$ and admit finite self-coproducts in $R_\Prism$.

papers.title: LQG solution for POMDP without estimating states: A minimum variance approach
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the control of discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) systems subject to incomplete and corrupted measurements. Specifically, we focus on designing a Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) controller without relying on explicit state estimation. By leveraging minimum variance duality, our approach allows the current control input to be represented as a linear function of available measurements and previously applied inputs, successfully reducing the task to a tractable deterministic optimization problem. We provide theoretical justification for this framework and demonstrate its practical effectiveness through numerical experiments.

papers.title: Flag Varieties of General Quiver Representations: Characteristic Classes and Semi-Invariants
papers.abstract: We study flags of subrepresentations of a general representation of a finite quiver. For each representation, its flag scheme is the zero scheme of a section of a quotient bundle on a product of partial flag varieties. We obtain the generic dimension and cycle class and equivariant localization formulas for Euler characteristics and parabolic Schubert coefficients. We further express these coefficients as finite signed sums of semi-invariant dimensions for auxiliary star quivers with inward and outward flag arms. In the acyclic one-step case, this is compatible with the result of Derksen--Schofield--Weyman, and the zero-dimensional case recovers their semi-invariant counting theorem. Examples treat matrix pencils and generalized Kronecker quivers.
papers.comments: 29 pages. v3. generalized to flags; title changed. Final version to appear IMRN

papers.title: Online Beck--Fiala Down to Logarithmic Sparsity
papers.abstract: The celebrated (offline) Beck--Fiala conjecture asserts that every matrix $A\in\{0,1\}^{n\times T}$ with at most $d$ nonzero entries in each column has discrepancy $O(\sqrt d)$. In this note, we consider the {\it online} version of the conjecture. For every fixed $η>0$, we give a randomized online algorithm that achieves $O_η(\sqrt d)$ prefix discrepancy for every fixed sequence of $d$-sparse vectors $a_t\in[-1,1]^n$, except with probability at most \[ C_ηT\exp\left[-\frac{c_ηd}{\log^{2+η}(ed)}\right]. \] In particular, this gives an optimal $O(\sqrt d)$ discrepancy upper bound for $d\geq C_η(\log T)(\log\log T)^{2+η}$. This range of sparsity is optimal up to $\log\log T$ factors. The result also resolves in strong form the {\it online Spencer problem}, corresponding to the case $d = n$. The algorithm is based on a compactly supported Metropolis walk, constructed by combining ideas from several recent works on online vector balancing. The proof was generated in conversation with ChatGPT 5.6 Pro; the authors provided high-level guidance in several rounds of prompting, followed by manual checking and rewriting of the proof.
papers.comments: Minor revision - simplified proof and significantly expanded the exposition

papers.title: A Minimax Analysis of the Last Iterate of the SubGradient Method in Finite Dimension
papers.abstract: We study the last iterate of the projected subGradient Method with a constant stepsize for convex $L$-Lipschitz objectives in $\mathbb{R}^d$, minimized over closed convex sets. Assuming that the initial iterate $x_1$ has distance at most $R$ from a minimizer, we establish matching upper and lower bounds on the minimax optimization error at $x_n$, where the infimum is taken over constant stepsizes. Specifically, this error is of order $L\cdot R\cdot\sqrt{\min\{d,\log n\}/n}$. Notably, when the dimension is fixed, the minimax error decays as $1/\sqrt{n}$, without the extra logarithmic factor intrinsic to dimension-free analyses. Our analysis exploits a combinatorial argument based on linear algebra and novel geometric constructions.
papers.comments: 25 pages, 2 figures. Substantially revised and expanded; sharp minimax bounds after optimizing over constant stepsizes. Title and abstract updated

papers.title: Automated Numerical Stability Analysis of Deep Learning Operators
papers.abstract: Finite-precision arithmetic unavoidably introduces numerical approximation errors. Numerical computations may use insufficient precision or an improper formulation, which leads to numerical instability. In this paper, we introduce a unified software tool for stochastic numerical validation of deep-learning operators. The tool follows CESTAC on supported exposed operations and uses an operator-level data-perturbation approximation for GEMM-like kernels. Our developed software not only enables numerical validation with a single computation pass but also detects the sources of numerical instability and provides numerical stability monitoring during deep learning training and inference. We verified its effectiveness on the detection of polluted operators with injected numerical instabilities across various tasks. We believe that our developed method and tools provide valuable insights into developing numerically stable computing kernels, which are particularly critical for numerically stable and efficient deep learning training and inference.

papers.title: An infinitesimal deformation of the post-Lie and post-Hopf algebra correspondence
papers.abstract: We describe infinitesimal deformations of post-Lie algebras and post-Hopf algebras and prove that the universal enveloping algebra and primitive elements adjunction is compatible with the infinitesimal structure. In characteristic zero, this restricts to an equivalence for connected cocommutative infinitesimal post-Hopf algebras, extending the Cartier--Milnor--Moore theorem. We parametrize all infinitesimal post-Lie structures on $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ and exhibit a second-order obstruction. From a geometric point of view, infinitesimal post-Lie algebras emerge from flat connections with covariantly constant torsion and an additional compatible symmetric $(1,2)$-tensor. This leads to explicit examples of infinitesimal post-Lie structures based on Heisenberg Lie algebras. On the Hopf side, we classify infinitesimal structures above the trivial action, prove rigidity for group algebras, and describe the structures on Sweedler's Hopf algebra. The subadjacent construction induces a Hopf algebra deformation with fixed coproduct. Finally, we prove that the quadratic operad of infinitesimal post-Lie algebras is Koszul, using a filtered distributive law between the operads of Lie algebras and bi-magmas.
papers.comments: Correction of Theorem 15, improvement of Section 2.1.3, other minor additions and updated references

papers.title: Domain-Adaptive Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding for Image Classification
papers.abstract: Deep joint source--channel coding (Deep JSCC) can suffer from domain shift between training and deployment data. We study single-source domain adaptation for image classification over wireless channels. A Gaussian example shows that improving channel quality does not necessarily improve target-domain accuracy under a fixed source-trained classifier. We further proposed an information objective to reduce domain information while preserving class information. Motivated by the analysis, we develop a domain-adaptive Deep JSCC method that combines class-wise adversarial alignment with pseudo-label supervised contrastive learning. The former uses all target samples to reduce class-conditional domain differences, while the latter selects high-confidence target samples to obtain class-discriminative received representations. We relate these losses to the information objective, and analyze the effects of pseudo-label errors and confidence-based selection. Experiments on SVHN--MNIST and PACS over AWGN and Rayleigh channels demonstrate improved target-domain classification without additional inference-time networks. The proposed method achieves 98.15\% accuracy on SVHN $\rightarrow$ MNIST at 10~dB CSNR.

papers.title: 2-Linearizability of Geometric 3-Manifold Groups Over Commutative Rings
papers.abstract: The fundamental groups of compact 3-manifolds are known to be residually finite. Feng Luo conjectured that a stronger statement is true, by only allowing finite groups of the form $\mathrm{PGL}(2,R)$, where $R$ is a finite commutative ring. In earlier work, this conjecture was disproven in full generality. The conjecture arose in the context of orientable connected compact 3-manifolds which are geometrizable. By constructing explicit faithful linear representations using rings with nilpotent elements, we demonstrate that the conjecture holds for six of the eight Thurston model geometries, namely all but $\mathbb{S}^3$ and $\widetilde{\mathrm{SL}_2}$. In the case of $\mathbb{S}^3$, the conjecture holds if we replace $\mathrm{PGL}(2,R)$ with $\mathrm{GL}(2,R)$. A spherical counterexample for the projective variant is the Poincaré homology sphere $Σ(2,3,5)$. In the case of $\widetilde{\mathrm{SL}_2}$, the conjecture fails to hold for both the projective and non-projective variants; a counterxample is provided by the Brieskorn sphere $Σ(2,3,7)$.

papers.title: $0/1$-Polytopes with Exponentially Small Edge Expansion
papers.abstract: We present a simple construction of a family of $0/1$-polytopes whose edge expansion decreases exponentially with the dimension, which disproves the Mihail-Vazirani conjecture that the graph of every $0/1$-polytope has edge expansion at least one.

papers.title: Many Antipodal Pairs Force Many Neighboring Pairs
papers.abstract: Let $X=\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of points of diameter at most $1$. It is natural to expect that if many pairs $(x_i,x_j)$ lie at distance close to $1$ from each other, then some clustering phenomenon must occur, implying that a significant number of these pairs are also very close to each other. %For $0<\varepsilon<1$, we call a pair $(x_i,x_j)$ $\varepsilon$-antipodal if $\|x_i-x_j\|\ge 1-\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon$-neighboring if $\|x_i-x_j\|\le \varepsilon$. We prove that there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that for all $0<\varepsilon<1$, whenever $n$ is large enough, we have: \[ \big|\{(i,j):\|x_i-x_j\|\le \varepsilon\}\big| \geq c\cdot \varepsilon^{1/2}\cdot \big|\{(i,j):\|x_i-x_j\|\geq 1-\varepsilon\}\big|. \] This confirms a recent conjecture of Steinerberger, who asked whether the $\varepsilon^{1/2}$ ratio is the best possible. We also study a two-parameter version of Steinerberger's question by considering the number of pairs at distance at most $\varepsilon_1$ and at distance at least $1-\varepsilon_2$. We show that in this case the optimal ratio is $\varepsilon_1^2\cdot\varepsilon_2^{-3/2}$ when $\varepsilon_1\leq\varepsilon_2$, and $\varepsilon_1^{1/2}$ otherwise. The proof proceeds by introducing an auxiliary graph associated with the set $X$ and reducing the problem to bounding the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix. Our main result is the outcome of human--AI interactions using ChatGPT 5.4.

papers.title: Universality in random graphs via optimal linking systems: trees and beyond
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for proving universality results in sparse random graphs. As a first application, we show that there exists an absolute constant $C>1$ such that, with high probability, for every fixed constant $Δ$, the binomial random graph $G(n,C\ln n/n)$ contains every $n$-vertex tree with maximum degree at most $Δ$. This answers a question of Montgomery (Advances in Mathematics, 2019). We also determine, for every $p$ satisfying $C\ln n/n\leq p=n^{-1+o(1)}$, the minimum girth $\ell$ (up to an absolute multiplicative constant) for which with high probability $G(n,p)$ contains all cycle factors of girth at least $Ω(\ell)$. In particular, with high probability $G(n,C\ln n/n)$ contains all cycle factors of girth at least $C\ln n/\ln\ln n$, which is optimal up to a constant factor. This extends an earlier result of Ferber, Kronenberg, and Luh (Transactions of the American Mathematical Society, 2019) and significantly improves a corollary of a deep result of Kahn, Lubetzky, and Wormald (Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics, 2017). One of the key ingredients in the proofs is establishing the optimal depth of linking systems in sparse random graphs.

papers.title: A Torelli-type theorem for hyperkähler quotients
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the moduli space of algebraic asymptotic hyperkähler structures on hyperkähler quotients arising from a quaternionic vector space $\mathbb{H}^n$. We consider the period map on this moduli space, and prove a Torelli-type theorem (i.e., the bijectivity of the period map) under mild assumptions including the surjectivity of the Kirwan map. This work provides an algebro-geometric generalization of the Torelli-type theorem for ALE gravitational instantons by Kronheimer (1989). In particular, this theorem applies to toric hyperkähler varieties and Nakajima quiver varieties.
papers.comments: 30 pages. v2: §4.5.2 (algebraicity via twistor spaces) revised

papers.title: Monoidal and symmetrized parametrized topological complexity
papers.abstract: We introduce and study monoidal and symmetrized versions of parametrized topological complexity. First, we develop parametrized analogues of the monoidal topological complexity theories of Iwase--Sakai, Aguilar-Guzmán--González (based on the Fadell--Husseini approach), and Dranishnikov. We investigate the parametrized Iwase--Sakai conjecture and provide sufficient conditions under which it holds. We then introduce symmetrized parametrized topological complexity and combine it with the monoidal perspective to define monoidal symmetrized parametrized topological complexity, showing that the resulting notions agree. Finally, we compute these invariants for Fadell--Neuwirth fibrations.
papers.comments: 38 pages. Generalized Proposition 4.4 (fiberwise homotopy invariance of symmetrized parametrized TC) to different bases. Corrected computations for Fadell--Neuwirth fibrations by proving Lemmas 6.2 and 6.3

papers.title: The $β=2$ partition function of Dirichlet $L$-functions and typical maxima
papers.abstract: We study the $β=2$ partition function $\int_{|h| \leq \log ^θ q/2}|L(1/2+ih,χ)|^2dh$ for typical Dirichlet characters modulo a large prime $q$ and $θ\in (-1/3,0]$ motivated by a $q$-analogue of the Saksman--Webb conjectures. When $θ<0$, we use an extension of Harper's randomisation argument with different localisations to recover moment upper bounds consistent with the critical normalisation predicted there. As an application, we prove that for $q(1-o(1))$ Dirichlet characters modulo $q$ with $U(q) \to \infty$, $$\max_{|h| \leq 1/2}|L(1/2+ih,χ)|\ll \frac{e^{U(q)}\log q\log_3 q(\log_4 q)^{1/2}}{(\log_2 q)^{3/4}},$$ establishing an upper bound matching the predictions of the $q$-analogue of the Fyodorov--Hiary--Keating conjectures up to second order. Our proofs adapt Harper's argument in \cite{harper2019partition}.
papers.comments: 35 pages. Fixed multiple issues in Sections 4 and 5, reworked the proofs and better exposition. Comments welcome

papers.title: Intersective Polynomials and Universal Separation of Divosor Profiles
papers.abstract: We classify universal divisor-profile separation for coprime polynomial pairs of arbitrary degree and for all pairs of degree at most two. For \(A\subset\N\) and \(m\in\Z\), let \(d_A(m)\) count the members of \(A\) dividing \(m\). For coprime nonzero \(F,G\in\Z[x]\), universally unbounded separation between \(d_A(F(n))\) and \(d_A(G(n))\) occurs if and only if one of \(F,G\) is intersective, that is, has a root modulo every positive integer. More generally, an intersective factor separated from finitely many polynomial opponents yields simultaneous one-sided dominance against all of them. For pairs with common irreducible factors, let \(U,V\) be the products of the factors occurring only on the two respective sides. Universal separation forces \(UV\) to have a root modulo almost every prime; equivalently, its Galois action has no derangement. We resolve the remaining finite \(p\)-adic boundary for all pairs of degree at most two: separation holds exactly when \(UV\) and at least one of \(F,G\) are intersective, and the criterion is unchanged by contents or factor multiplicities. The same criterion holds, in arbitrary degree, for three linear support factors with arbitrary positive multiplicities. The proofs combine uniform almost-prime values on root progressions with an adaptive local-routing argument.

papers.title: Indefinite integrals of Bessel and Struve functions with half-integer indices, and incomplete gamma functions with integer indices, all multiplied by $Exp(-ax^{2})$ and divided by powers
papers.abstract: Indefinite integrals are found for 63 half-integer Bessel and Struve functions, and incomplete gamma functions with integer indices, each multiplied by $Exp(-ax^{2})$ and divided by powers. A series solution is given for the individual terms (of any inverse power) in such functions, split into even and odd portions. Eight integrals are given involving these series. Three infinite sets of auxiliary integrals are also given.

papers.title: Witt groups of smooth real curves and surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the $\mathbf{I}^*$-cohomology of a smooth real algebraic curve in terms of its real locus and its geometric genus. We notably extend results of Knebusch and Monnier to the twisted case. We further describe how to compute twisted Witt groups of surfaces, generalising work of Sujatha, and apply our results to the computation of the shifted and twisted Witt groups of the smooth real anisotropic quadric surface. Finally, we extend Monnier's investigation of the image of the global signature homomorphism for surfaces.
papers.comments: 31 pages. v4: greatly streamlined, study of (Chow--)Witt groups of quadrics reduced to the Witt groups of the smooth real anisotropic surface, removed investigation of Pardon spectral sequence, comments still welcome

papers.title: Borelness of Moduli Spaces of Metrics Implies Separability
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a metrizable space, and let $\mathrm{Met}(X)$ denote the space of metrics compatible with the topology of $X$, regarded as a subspace of the space of continuous pseudometrics with the topology induced by the supremum metric. We first prove that if $Z$ is a discrete space whose cardinality is the first uncountable cardinal, then $\mathrm{Met}(Z)$ is not Borel. As a consequence, if $\mathrm{Met}(X)$ is Borel, then $X$ is separable. Combined with a theorem of Koshino, our result yields that the space of bounded compatible metrics on a metrizable space $X$ is completely metrizable if and only if $X$ is $σ$-compact. We also establish non-Archimedean analogues for spaces of ultrametrics. We further prove componentwise versions of these results, where two metrics belong to the same component if their distance is finite.

papers.title: A Note on Topological Hochschild Homology Relative to $\Sphere_{W(k)}[x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n]$
papers.abstract: We explain the relation between the relative topological Hochschild homology $\THH(R/\Sphere_{W(k)}[x_0,\ldots,x_n])$ and the Nygaard-completed Frobenius-twisted relative prismatic cohomology $\widehat{\Prism}^{(1)}_{R/W(k)[x_0,\ldots,x_n]^\wedge}$, where $W(k)[x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n]\rightarrow R$ is relatively quasiregular semiperfectoid. As an application, for $R=\Z_p[x]/(px)$, we compute $π_*\THH(R)^\wedge_p$ by descent along $\THH(R)^\wedge_p\rightarrow \THH(R/\Sphere_p[z,x])$, where $R$ is regarded as an $\Einfty$-$\Sphere_p[z,x]$-algebra via $\Sphere_p[z,x]\xrightarrow{z\mapsto p,x\mapsto x}\Z_p[x]/(px)$.

papers.title: A Layered Simplex Architecture for Large Alphabets
papers.abstract: A learning architecture induces a prior over its expressible models. Recent work links architectural success to a broad complexity spectrum: model probabilities spanning many orders of magnitude. Understanding how depth shapes these priors and prediction may help explain the success of neural networks and transformers. We study this connection in large-alphabet prediction through the *layered simplex architecture* (LSA), which multiplies independent uniform simplex vectors coordinate-wise and normalizes. At depth zero, the prior is concentrated on the uniform distribution; at depth one, the Bayesian predictor is Laplace's rule. Each additional layer shifts prior mass toward more concentrated distributions. We derive exact Bayesian marginal likelihood and regret expressions using reusable depth-specific kernels. Mixing over depths up to a cutoff logarithmic in alphabet size yields an explicit predictor with rigorous guarantees. For targets uniform on a specified sparse support, the mixture's prior complexity is asymptotic to the support-description cost at every fixed positive KL resolution, establishing a broad complexity spectrum. We also prove a regret lower bound for every label-invariant predictor: the expected description length of the discovered symbol set minus the source's uncertainty about its identity given its size. For Zipf sources in a growing-alphabet regime, the depth mixture attains this bound to leading order. Thus, the symbol-discovery rate determines the regret exponent. Although introduced to study depth, the LSA predictor competes with established large-alphabet methods, including Good--Turing, Ristad's law and an adaptive Dirichlet mixture, while substantially outperforming classical add-constant rules on concentrated sources.

papers.abstract:

The quasilinear structure leads to unavoidable derivative loss, which prevents the direct construction of solutions via iteration of the Duhamel formula. For $σ\in(1,2]$, we prove that, with high probability, solutions exist up to time scales ${T} \simα^{-{ rac43}+} \wedge α^{- rac1{σ/2-β}+}$, and that only trivial four-wave resonances occur, leading to a degenerate wave kinetic equation. For $σ\in(0,1)$, we prove the existence up to time scales $T\sim α^{- rac43+}$, and show that the second-order statistics are well approximated by the wave kinetic equation. In both cases, the solutions remain smooth while exhibiting smallness in suitable $L^\infty$-based norms. The proof combines propagation of randomness for a truncated equation with deterministic energy estimates and a bootstrap argument. The main technical difficulties arise in the regime $σ\in(0,1)$. At low frequencies, the counting argument requires simultaneous control of the frequency gap and the associated resonant phase gap. In the energy estimate, nontrivial resonances generate quartic terms that prevent the energy estimates from closing the bootstrap on $[0,T]$. To overcome this obstruction, we develop a new normal-form $L^2$ energy estimates, using distinct frequency truncations for the initial data and the nonlinearity.

papers.title: The Cesàro Operator, Rhaly operators, and the Toeplitz Algebra
papers.abstract: Barría and Halmos [\emph{Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.} (1982), (10) Example] asked whether the Cesàro operator belongs to the Toeplitz algebra. We answer this question affirmatively and prove that the Cesàro operator is the product of a Toeplitz operator and a continuous function of a self-adjoint Toeplitz operator. Rhaly operators are a natural generalization of the Cesàro operator. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for a Rhaly operator to belong to the Toeplitz algebra or the Hankel algebra. The main approach is to use the Fejér kernels to get localized estimates for operators. This yields a necessary condition for an operator to belong to the Hankel algebra. As an application, we find a class of Rhaly operators that are asymptotic Toeplitz operators and essentially commute with the unilateral shift, but are not in the Hankel algebra. This answers (17) Question in the same paper.

papers.title: Distributed Cross-Layer Optimization for Covert Multi-Hop, Multi-Modal Networks: Exponentially Fast Convergence and Robust Tracking
papers.abstract: This paper develops the first distributed cross-layer algorithm for joint congestion control, routing, scheduling, and power control in covert multi-hop, multi-modal wireless networks, where adversarial wardens (Willies) monitor radio modalities via energy detection. The Detection Error Probability (DEP), the probability that a Willie fails to reliably detect ongoing transmissions, is generally non-concave in the transmit powers, making DEP-based covert network optimization challenging. We resolve this by constructing the tightest concave lower bound on the log-DEP, yielding a conservative convex problem that guarantees satisfaction of the original DEP constraints and unifies hard covertness constraints and covertness-utility maximization in a single problem. We develop a Parallel Proximal Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (PP-ADMM) algorithm for the resulting cross-layer problem and prove global Q-linear convergence, i.e., exponentially fast convergence, to the set of optimal solutions under standard regularity conditions. Numerical results confirm linear convergence and demonstrate robust tracking performance under channel fading and Willie mobility.
papers.comments: 18 pages, 6 figures. Full technical report corresponding to the paper accepted to IEEE MILCOM 2026

papers.title: On the Brill--Noether Theory of Sheaves on Regular Surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the Brill--Noether theory of higher rank sheaves on surfaces $X$ with $H^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X) = 0$ and its interactions with the classical Brill--Noether theory of line bundles on curves lying on $X$. Denoting by $\mathrm{Spl}(v)$ the moduli space of simple sheaves on $X$ with Chern character $v = (r,c_1,\mathrm{ch}_2)$, we introduce the Brill--Noether loci $BN^k(v)^\circ \subseteq \mathrm{Spl}(v)$ of \emph{generically $k$-generated} sheaves and show, under assumptions on $c_1$ and $K_X$, certain well-behavedness results. In particular, if $c_1$ is \emph{indecomposable} and $X$ is a K3 surface, we generalize a Brill--Noether theorem for sheaves on K3s due to Yoshioka. This is achieved by employing He's deformation theory of the moduli space of coherent systems and a globalization of the Lazarsfeld--Mukai construction, providing a correspondence between the Brill--Noether theories of generically $r$-generated sheaves on $X$ and that of line bundles on curves $C \in |c_1|$. The same techniques yield upper bounds on the dimension of $\mathcal{W}^{r,\mathrm{bpf}}_d(|c_1|) \setminus \mathcal{W}^{r+1}_d(|c_1|)$ consisting of basepoint-free line bundles in terms of the number of endomorphisms of associated Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, for arbitrary $c_1$. This generalizes a result of Aprodu and Farkas in the context of Green's conjecture beyond K3 surfaces. In the case $r = 1$ of pencils, we obtain smoothness and expected-dimension results under an effectivity condition on $-K_X|_C$ for $C \in |c_1|$. As an application, we prove Green's conjecture for the general curve on a rational surface with a nef and effective anticanonical divisor.

papers.title: Markov Chain CLTs: Resolving Open Problems
papers.abstract: Markov chain central limit theorems (CLTs) and their associated variances are very important for implementing Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms among other applications. Häggström and Rosenthal (2007) presented various results regarding the equality of different formulae for this variance and also posed seven open problems. We resolve all seven in this paper. Our main result is a general characterization of Markov chain CLTs: for stationary and ergodic Markov chains, we prove that the normalized partial sums satisfy a $\sqrt{n}$-CLT if and only if the Poisson equation admits a finite solution with square-integrable martingale differences whose second moment equals the CLT variance. In particular, this result does not require reversibility of the chain or square integrability of the function. It implies that Roberts' holding-probability condition always precludes a $\sqrt{n}$-CLT, and for reversible chains, whenever a $\sqrt{n}$-CLT holds, the variance limit is finite if the function is square-integrable, otherwise undefined. In addition, we develop a general principle that expresses Fourier coefficients as the autocovariances of an ergodic nonreversible Markov chain.

papers.title: Noncommutative sharp Hausdorff-Young inequality
papers.abstract: We prove the sharp Hausdorff--Young inequality on quantum euclidean spaces. Our result implies the sharp Hausdorff--Young constants for the Weyl transform. The key ingredients are a sharp Hessian comparison inequality and a novel flow related to the mixed- norm of noncommutative Gabor transform; the Hessian comparison leads to the monotonicity of the flow. We also apply the same flow technique to prove the sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities on Heisenberg groups and the affine group.
papers.comments: Submitted version. This manuscript was submitted to the journal in mid-Oct.,2026

papers.title: Free-Probabilistic State Evolution and Random Matrix Discrepancy
papers.abstract: Let $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ be independent $d \times d$ real symmetric Gaussian random matrices, and consider the linear operator $A(x) = n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i$, $x\in \mathbb R^n$. We construct an iterative algorithm in the Approximate Message Passing family which iterates over $A$ and its adjoint $A^*$, and establish a state evolution result which characterizes its behavior in the limit $d\to \infty, 2n/d^2 \to α$ in terms of a correlated Gaussian-semicircular process in a free probability space, in the sense of strong convergence of operators. We then apply this iteration to the random matrix discrepancy problem which asks for a binary vector $x \in \{-1,+1\}^n$ such that $A(x)$ has a small operator norm. Our algorithm achieves an operator norm $2σ(α)$, for a standard deviation $σ(α)<1$ for all $α>0$, and $σ(α) = O(1/\sqrt{α\log α})$ for large $α$. This resolves the algorithmic question of Kunisky-Zhang (2023) and Maillard (2025).
papers.comments: Revised version contains stronger results on random matrix discrepancy, further minor edits, and an updated bibliography

papers.title: Confusion-Erasure Bounds of Error-Bounded Decoders under QAM
papers.abstract: 6G is expected to push ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) toward stringent residual-error tar- gets for mission-critical services, where undetected errors and erasures carry fundamentally different costs. Block error rate (BLER) conflates block confusions (undetected errors) and block erasures, which have fundamentally different impacts on system reliability. To characterize the confusion rate analyt- ically, we consider an error-bounded decoder with spherical decision regions. We focus on square quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) constellations in the finite blocklength (FBL) regime. The confusion rate is governed by the Euclidean distances between modulated codewords, whereas the code structure constrains their Hamming distances. To bridge the two metrics, we introduce a typical distance, which represents the Euclidean distance of a codeword pair at a given Hamming distance on average, and relate it to the Hamming distance through a per-symbol squared-distance coefficient. On this basis, we derive a lower bound on the block confusion rate for random codes and an upper bound for codebooks whose minimum Euclidean distance reaches the typical distance at the non-overlapping threshold. We further characterize how both bounds evolve with the average symbol energy and the block- length. Numerical results, validated by an exact computation for short codes, confirm that as the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) or redundancy increases, the confusion rate falls many orders of magnitude below the reliability target, leaving detectable erasures as the dominant residual error.

papers.title: Long-Time Dispersion and Threshold Resonances for the Landau Hamiltonian on the Hyperbolic Plane
papers.abstract: A uniform magnetic field completely suppresses long-time dispersion for the Euclidean Landau Hamiltonian. We show that negative curvature fundamentally changes this behavior. For the Landau Hamiltonian with arbitrary field strength $B\in\mathbb R$ on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb H$, we establish sharp dispersive estimates for the Schrödinger evolution on the absolutely continuous spectral subspace. The decay is $|t|^{-1}$ at short times and, strikingly, improves to $|t|^{-3/2}$ at large times whenever $B\notin\frac12+\mathbb Z$. At half-integer fields, we identify a threshold resonance and isolate its leading contribution, which yields the slower but sharp rate $|t|^{-1/2}$. Thus the long-time dynamics exhibit a resonance-driven dichotomy with no analogue in the flat constant-field problem. Our analysis is based on an explicit representation of the magnetic Schrödinger kernel together with a precise separation of the Landau levels and threshold profile. As a further consequence, for every nonthreshold field we obtain global-in-time Strichartz estimates on the absolutely continuous spectral subspace throughout the full hyperbolic admissible region.

papers.title: An explicit solution of the five-expert prediction PDE and the exact optimality set of COMB
papers.abstract: In this paper, we derive an explicit solution of the stationary prediction with expert advice PDE for five experts. The formula is given in three regions. In the first two regions, it is the four-expert solution plus a single integral with an elementary positive density. In the third region, it is a finite sum of hyperbolic products whose coefficients are determined by one scalar quadrature. Our formula establishes that the rank ordered adversary $(1,0,1,0,0)$ achieves the Hamiltonian maximum in the PDE everywhere in the ordered sector, while the COMB strategy $(1,0,1,0,1)$ is optimal only on a lower dimensional subset of the sector (where $x_1=x_2$ and $x_3=x_4$). The verification of the Hamiltonian inequalities is a tedious task, part of which is completed with a computer assisted proof. The verification reduces to 21 scalar inequalities, which we prove using 147 exact rational Bernstein polynomial certificates. The exact certificates and their independent arithmetic checks are included in a supplement to this paper, and a Lean 4 formalization machine-checks the verification and both main theorems, apart from the viscosity characterization.

papers.title: A Cheeger Inequality for Hypergraphs and Its Applications
papers.abstract: Hypergraphs provide a natural framework for modeling higher-order relationships, but the development of spectral techniques with provable guarantees for general non-uniform hypergraphs remains challenging. Building on Banerjee's normalized adjacency matrix and Spiro's averaging-based diffusion framework, we develop a spectral framework for non-uniform hypergraphs and establish Cheeger's inequality for their conductance. A fundamental result in the spectral theory of hypergraphs asserts that, for every non-covering hypergraph, the second-smallest eigenvalue of its normalized Laplacian is at most one. This spectral characterization yields an improved Cheeger's inequality for non-covering hypergraphs, and we show that the resulting inequality is tight on both sides using cycle and cube hypergraphs. Our framework further yields higher-order Cheeger inequalities and provides theoretical guarantees for Fiedler's spectral partitioning algorithm, all in the setting of hypergraphs. Finally and most notably, we construct a new family of optimal hypergraph expanders that is tight for the Alon-Boppana bound.

papers.title: The Aldous chain on cladograms mixes in order $n^2$ steps
papers.abstract: Cladograms of size $n$ are unrooted binary trees whose leaves are labelled from 1 to $n$. Aldous introduced in 2000 a Markov chain on cladograms, a step of which consists of removing a leaf uniformly at random and reinserting it on a uniformly chosen edge. We introduce a coupling for this walk, which follows multiple colored subtrees in parallel. We go around the lack of independence of the colored components by finding a relevant statistic, namely the sum of the squares of the sizes of all colored components, which we prove has a drift. We deduce that the mixing time of the walk is of order $n^2$, solving a conjecture of Aldous.

papers.title: Monge's transport problem in synthetic Lorentzian spacetimes
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of solutions to the Lorentzian Monge problem on synthetic Lorentzian spacetimes that satisfy the forward timelike measure contraction property $TMCP^+(K,N)$. The cost for this problem is the time separation function $\ell(x,y)$ (the Lorentz distance), which represents the maximum amount a particle can age when traveling from $x$ to $y$. The solution is based on the needle decomposition technique, and amounts to a reduction of the full problem to its one-dimensional counterparts. As an application of needle decomposition, we introduce the blended $TMCP$ condition, and obtain a quantitative refinement of the synthetic Hawking singularity theorem. We additionally prove a timelike nonbranching reversibility theorem for $TCD_p(K,N)$ spacetimes, showing that forward $p$-essentially nonbranching spacetimes are backward $p$-essentially nonbranching.

papers.title: Physical and emergent nonpairwise interactions in oscillator networks: from higher-order phase reduction to coupling design
papers.abstract: Phase reduction is a powerful technique to obtain phase models from high dimensional oscillatory systems. Starting from pairwise interactions, a first order approximation yields Kuramoto and Winfree phase models, while nonpairwise interactions emerge at the second order. Recently, phase models have been extended to account for nonpairwise interactions, notably, the higher-order Kuramoto model. Is there an intrinsic difference between physical and emergent nonpairwise interactions? And can we make use of the former to even out the effects of the latter? In this work, we exploit a recently developed parametrization method to compute the phase reduction and answer these questions. After a comparison of the new method with the classic Kuramoto-style phase reduction, we derive the network motifs of the emergent nonpairwise interactions and compare them with the physical once. Lastly, we exploit the motifs to adopt a coupling design approach. Our framework paves the way for further exploitations of physical nonpairwise interactions for applications in synchronization engineering.

papers.title: The First-Order Oracle Complexity of Lipschitz Convex Optimization in Nondual Settings
papers.abstract: We study first-order black-box convex optimization over an $\ell_p$-ball for objectives Lipschitz in the $\ell_q$-norm, solving in the affirmative the nonsmooth version of the COLT open question (Guz15b) on whether the geometry of a smaller feasible set ($p < q$) can improve convergence rates in convex optimization, and matching prior lower bounds up to logarithmic factors. Our rates include $\widetilde{O}(1/T)$ for convex Euclidean-Lipschitz optimization over the $\ell_1$-ball, improving on the $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ classical rate under general assumptions. The key technical device is a new online learning game, where the comparator is evaluated using the maximum of affine losses observed so far. We bound the value of this game above and below in terms of a combinatorial online learning quantity: the sequential fat-shattering dimension, which we characterize for the $\ell_p / \ell_q$ case. Our results generally apply when the feasible set $\mathcal{X}$ and the set of possible subgradients $\mathcal{H}$ admit a type of minimax theorem, advancing on a fundamental question by Sridharan (Sri12, Section 10.1.2, Q3). As a geometric consequence of our analysis, of independent interest, we obtain estimates for the expected distance of a convex hull of samples to their mean in several Banach geometries, a version of the celebrated Wendel's theorem (Wen62), but quantitative and for bounded general distributions as opposed to centrally symmetric ones.
papers.comments: Polished writing. Small additions (quasar-convex optimization, clarification regarding optimizing in a subset...)

papers.title: Stable Movement for Nondual Lipschitz Convex Optimization: Efficiency and Nearly Optimal Oracle Rates
papers.abstract: We study efficient algorithms for realizing the first-order oracle complexity of optimization of $G$-Lipschitz convex functions with respect to the $\ell_q$-norm over an $\ell_p$-ball of radius $R$, where $1\leq p,q\leq\infty$. For $p<q$, we obtain error $\widetilde{O}_{p,q}(GR/T^{1/p-(1/q-1/2)_{+}})$ after $T$ oracle queries, attaining the lower bounds in a COLT 2015 open problem (Guz15b) with efficient algorithms. In particular, the rate is $\widetilde{O}(GR/T)$ for Euclidean Lipschitzness with an $\ell_1$-ball domain of radius $R$ ($p=1,q=2$). Our solution consists of reducing convex Lipschitz optimization to the chasing nested convex sets problem (BBE+20) in sublevel sets of an evolving maximum of affine lower bounds, that is, the bundle (LNN95): at each query we either find a point with low function value or we produce a deep cut in the current sublevel of the bundle that we chase. The dichotomy between stability of selectors and forced movement by deep cuts bounds the number of iterations of the algorithm nearly optimally. For nested convex subsets of the $\ell_p$ ball $R B_p^d$, we introduce novel stable selectors whose movement is nearly optimal in high dimensions. A Monte Carlo average of the proposed selector achieves near-optimal rates with high probability and can be implemented for our optimization algorithm in polynomial time in the real-arithmetic model.
papers.comments: polished writing, added a few more general results (such as a better lower bound, and a more general potential-energy center)

papers.title: Isogeometric analysis for the Helmholtz transmission eigenvalue problem
papers.abstract: The transmission eigenvalue problem plays an increasingly important role in inverse scattering theory. Although significant progress has been made in developing efficient numerical methods for the problem over the last two decades, its numerical treatment for curved domains in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d=2,3$) remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce and analyze a geometrically flexible and $H^2$-conforming isogeometric method for solving a fourth-order, quadratic and non-self-adjoint eigenvalue problem arising from the Helmholtz transmission eigenvalue problem. Using the spectral approximation theory for compact non-self-adjoint operators, we derive optimal error estimates for the discrete eigenvalues and eigenfunctions. Numerical results for the two- and three-dimensional benchmark problems, including those defined in curved domains, are presented to verify our theoretical results, and to demonstrate the advantages of the method over existing numerical methods in terms of both accuracy and geometric flexibility.

papers.title: Descent along flat composed with radicalization
papers.abstract: We study the following general situation. Let $R\to S$ be a finite flat morphism of regular rings of zero (resp. prime) mixed or (equi)-characteristic. For $P\in Spec R$, put $A=R/P, C=S/PS,$ and $B=S/\sqrt{PS}=C_{\mathrm{red}}.$ The basic question is whether a property of $B$ forces the same property of $A$. The main point is that ordinary finite-flat descent applies naturally to $A\to C$, whereas the passage $C\to C_{\mathrm{red}}$ may (not) destroy nilpotent information.

papers.title: $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has the Bogomolov property for canonical heights
papers.abstract: We show that for any number field $K$ and any rational map $f$ in $K(x)$ of degree at least $2$ that is not conjugate to a power, (signed) Chebyshev or CM Lattès map, $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has the strong Bogomolov property for the canonical height of $f$. Combined with former results of Amoroso-Zannier, Pottmeyer and Ratazzi, this implies that $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has the Bogomolov property for canonical heights of any rational map of degree at least $2$. We also classify the pairs $(f,α)$ whose backward orbit contains infinitely many abelian points. This settles the Andrews--Petsche conjecture in the greater generality of rational maps over a number field and infinite abelian subsets of backward orbits. The authors were led to the main idea of the proof in conversation with \emph{Astra}. The key insight consists of applying Yuan's equidistribution results, followed by a classification of $(f,f)$-preperiodic curves due to Pakovich and Beaumont followed by an additional application of equidistribution on a parametrized preperiodic curve.

papers.title: Word Length and Diameter in Permutation Groups
papers.abstract: In the binary diameter problem, the input consists of explicitly given permutations generating a finite group $G$ and a binary-encoded number $k$, and the question is whether every element of $G$ is a product of at most $k$ of the given generators. In the binary length problem, the input additionally contains a permutation $g \in G$, and the question is whether $g$ is such a product. We show that the binary diameter problem is PSPACE-complete, thereby confirming a conjecture of Lohrey and Rosowski (2023). Moreover, we show that PSPACE-hardness already holds for solvable groups of derived length at most 3, whereas the problem is $Π_2^{\mathrm{P}}$-complete for 2-step nilpotent groups. For the binary length problem, we establish a sharp complexity threshold: the problem is NP-complete for 2-step nilpotent groups, which extends a result of Lohrey and Rosowski for abelian groups, and PSPACE-complete for groups that are simultaneously 3-step nilpotent and metabelian, which strengthens the main result of Jerrum (1985). Finally, we show that the unary diameter problem, where $k$ is encoded in unary, is $Π_2^{\mathrm{P}}$-complete for generating sets of the full symmetric group, confirming another conjecture of Lohrey and Rosowski.

papers.title: Metric foundations of geometry
papers.abstract: A metric space is called all-set-homogeneous if every isometry between two of its subsets extends to an isometry of the whole space. We classify all-set-homogeneous length spaces: besides the classical examples, they include the universal metric trees of finite valence.

papers.title: Critical semilinear damped wave equations beyond moduli of continuity
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for semilinear classical damped wave equations with general nonnegative nondecreasing nonlinearities, without imposing a modulus-of-continuity structure or convexity. A Dini-type integral condition expressed directly in terms of the nonlinearity gives small data global in-time existence and extends the nonlinear framework of Ebert--Girardi--Reissig [Math. Ann. 378 (2020), 1311--1326]. When this Dini-type integral diverges and the effective total mass of the initial data is positive, convergence of the Keller--Osserman tail integral is necessary and sufficient for finite-time blow-up of the maximal mild Sobolev solution, particularly, divergence of the tail integral gives global grow-up. The resulting integral criteria distinguish the contributions of the nonlinearity near zero and at infinity in governing small data global in-time existence with diffusion decay, global grow-up, and finite-time blow-up.

papers.title: Universal Formulas for de Jonquières Loci and Equivariant Contact Problems
papers.abstract: Given a family of genus $g$ curves $f:Ψ\to S$ and a relative degree $d$ line bundle $L$ on $Ψ$ such that $f_*L$ is a vector bundle, the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(f_*L)$ is stratified by relative de Jonquières loci, which parameterize sections of $L$ with prescribed vanishing orders. We give universal formulas for the classes of these loci in terms of the relative $O(1)$ on $\mathbb{P}(f_*L)$ and tautological classes pulled back from the universal Picard stack $\mathrm{Pic}_g^d$. When $f$ is the family of lines in $\mathbb{P}^r$, we use the universal polynomials to compute $\mathrm{GL}_{r+1}$-equivariant classes of loci of hypersurfaces and complete intersections admitting lines with prescribed contact orders.
papers.comments: v2: 25 pages. Added additional assumption to Theorem 1.2, and additional Lemma 3.3

papers.title: Differential Recursions, Projective Discriminants, and Algebraic Generating Functions
papers.abstract: We study two hierarchies of bivariate generating functions defined by differential recursions: a self-dual hierarchy and a reduced-symmetry hierarchy. Their rational coefficient functions produce palindromic and anti-palindromic triangles, including OEIS A336110 and A140136. For general differential order $p$, the reduced hierarchy decomposes into $p-1$ Horn-type companions. An explicit differential intertwiner of order $p-3$ relates the last companion to the normalized self-dual generating function. The companions share a principal symbol and a rationally parametrized characteristic curve with a projective $S_3$ action. At $p=2$ this construction yields the Narayana quadratic. At $p=3$ the symmetry lifts to $S_4$: two algebraic sectors are edge resolvents of one quartic root configuration, and the nonsymmetric Gross--Witten--Wadia generating function has degree four. For $p=4$ and $p=5$ we derive algebraic equations of degrees six and eight, respectively, and find Galois groups $S_6$ and $S_8$ at generic specializations. At $p=6$ we verify a degree-ten specialization with Galois group $S_{10}$. Their discriminants exhibit a universal cubic characteristic factor and a squared lower-order factor. A boundary factorization explains the observed algebraic degrees and discriminant monomials. We formulate conjectures on algebraicity and Galois groups in the reduced hierarchy and identify a possible mechanism for transcendence in the higher self-dual hierarchy.

papers.title: A Lean~4 Framework for the Radii Polynomial Method
papers.abstract: Understanding nonlinear dynamics is central to many fields of study, yet most nonlinear systems are beyond the reach of closed-form solutions. Numerical simulation is then used to reveal dynamical structures before their existence can be established. This alone, however, leaves the validity of the computed solution unanswered. Rigorous numerical methods address this gap by combining computation with explicit analytic estimates. Among them, the radii polynomial approach, a Newton--Kantorovich type argument, turns a numerical approximation into a proof of existence and uniqueness of a true solution near that approximation. In previous practice, the verification of these inequalities relies on interval-arithmetic libraries and hand-derived algebraic bounds. In this paper, we present a framework for the radii polynomial method in the Lean~4, which turns numerical certificates into fully type-checked theorems about the true solution. A central challenge in this process is to manage the complexity of the formalization. Our approach begins with a family of problems and their common structure. The spaces in which the analysis takes place are developed through universal properties in suitable categories, with extension properties that characterize maps by their action on generators. These properties guide the design of a reusable interface such that problem-specific arguments concentrate on the numerical data and the algebraic bounds that distinguish one equation from another. We formalize a general radii polynomial theorem, develop weighted coefficient algebras and reusable operator estimates, connect finite computational checks to the hypotheses of the theorem, and establish the realization theorems that transport certified coefficient space zeros to analytic solutions of the original equations.

papers.title: Infinitesimal Hilbertianity for manifolds with Sobolev regular Riemannian metrics through uniform lower capacity bounds
papers.abstract: We prove that metric measure spaces arising from $2$-manifolds equipped with Riemannian metrics $g$ such that $g, g^{-1} \in L^\infty_{\rm loc} \cap W^{1,p}_{\rm loc}$ are infinitesimally Hilbertian. Along the way, we establish uniform lower $1$-capacity bounds of several $1$-dimensional subsets of $\R^2$.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Strong Roberson Conjecture
papers.abstract: We refute the Strong Roberson Conjecture, which asserts that adding any graph outside a graph class closed under minors and disjoint unions strictly increases the distinguishing power of homomorphism counts from that class. More precisely, we construct connected graphs $H$ for which homomorphism counts from graphs excluding $H$ as a minor determine the number of homomorphisms from $H$ to any target graph. We also refute the analogous conjecture with immersions in place of minors. The proof introduces a method for deriving exact homomorphism count dependence from modular equivalences. We obtain these modular equivalences for infinitely many primes using prime-order automorphisms and the corresponding orbit quotients. We complete the refutations by proving that suitable circulant graphs with two jump lengths and related cubic bipartite graphs exclude their corresponding orbit quotients as minors and immersions, respectively.
papers.comments: 24 pages. v2: expanded introduction, related work and conclusion; improved exposition throughout; smaller explicit counterexamples obtained

papers.title: Sharp Riesz capacity inequalities and the Pólya--Szegő conjecture
papers.abstract: For $n\geq2$ and $p\in(n-2,n)$, we prove that closed balls maximize the ratio of Riesz $p$-capacity to Newtonian capacity among all compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$. This resolves the classical Pólya--Szegő capacity ratio conjecture and its higher-dimensional extensions. For $n\geq4$, a sharp inequality for the ratio of Newtonian capacity to logarithmic capacity is established. All equality cases are characterized.

papers.title: Finite Stick Breaking Sequences
papers.abstract: In 1949, De Bruijn and Erdős considered infinite stick-breaking sequences. In this work, we consider finite sequences and prove that an infinite sequence that is due to De Bruijn, Erdős, and Toulmin is in some sense unique.

papers.title: Model-Based Koopman-Galerkin Lifting for Guaranteed H-Infinity Output Feedback Control of Nonlinear Systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a model-based Koopman-Galerkin framework for output-feedback control of nonlinear systems with known dynamics. With a suitable actuator augmentation, the finite-dimensional realization preserves the actuator dynamics and the constant input matrix. The approach is based on an exact decomposition of the lifted dynamics into an LTI system and a finite-order closure residual. It also applies to non-control-affine systems and allows dictionaries that do not span an invariant subspace. Regional bounds are derived for the closure residual, actuator-realization defect, and output-reconstruction error. We use these bounds to formulate a standard $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ output-feedback problem. The controller is linear and dynamic and is implemented using only the measured tracking error. Neither full-state measurements nor a separate state observer are required. Lifting is performed offline. With the state coordinates retained in the dictionary, we obtain explicit transient bounds on the original state and tracking error. A sufficient condition for regional containment is also given. Under this condition, the nonlinear closed loop is forward complete, and the state and tracking error are uniformly ultimately bounded. The cart-pendulum example illustrates the nonlinear closed-loop guarantees. The proposed output feedback gives lower RMSE and peak tracking error on average than Jacobian-based $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ feedback, full-state backstepping, and Koopman-based hybrid MPC.

papers.title: When Hilbert functions determine generic initial ideals
papers.abstract: Over a field of characteristic zero, we characterize the Hilbert functions that determine the degree reverse lexicographic generic initial ideal among Artinian quotients of embedding dimension $n\ge2$ with the $(n-2)$-strong Lefschetz property. The criterion is a finite arithmetic test on successive positive differences of the Hilbert function. It uses recursively defined integer vectors and requires no construction of a monomial ideal. When uniqueness holds, the same vectors recover the common generic initial ideal degree by degree. The proof reduces uniqueness successively to uniqueness of lower sets of specified cardinalities in Borel orders. In four variables, the test simplifies to avoidance of explicitly computed integer intervals.
