We study this tradeoff through the design of fixed, personalized menus from which patients choose providers. We show that constructing the optimal menu is NP-hard and establish an information-theoretic lower bound. We find that offering each patient a single provider matches this bound up to a constant factor, while unrestricted choice can perform arbitrarily poorly. However, we show that additional choice improves on single-provider assignment when the system cannot reliably distinguish among a patient's alternatives. We formalize this tradeoff through two forms of loss: menu loss, which arises when menus offer too few options, and coordination loss, which arises when scarce capacity is exposed to too much choice. Motivated by this decomposition, we develop the Scenario-Averaged Marginals (SAM) algorithm, which tailors menus based on provider shadow prices so choice is offered only when utility exceeds the capacity cost. We identify sufficient conditions which SAM's regret matches the lower bound, namely when patients have valuable alternatives and offered menus don't create competition for scarce capacity. In a semi-synthetic environment calibrated to a provider network using Medicare data, SAM improves total utility by up to 19% over single-provider assignment as preference uncertainty grows, while improving utility for the least-served ZIP codes.

papers.title: Data-Efficient Kernel Methods for Learning Differential Equations and Their Solution Operators: Algorithms and Error Analysis
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel kernel-based framework for learning differential equations and their solution maps. The framework is efficient in its data requirements in terms of the number of observed states and the amount of data available per state. Our formulation also allows us to employ efficient Gauss-Newton-type optimization algorithms in the training procedure to improve accuracy and speed of the training procedure. We also support our algorithm with rigorous theoretical guarantees in the form of quantitative worst-case error bounds for the learned equation that can be extended to the subsequent solution operators under smoothness assumptions. Numerical benchmarks demonstrate significant improvements in computational complexity and robustness while achieving one to two orders of magnitude improvements in terms of accuracy compared to certain state-of-the-art algorithms.

papers.title: Conformal-DP: A Density-Aware Mechanism for Differential Privacy over Riemannian Manifolds via Conformal Transformation
papers.abstract: Differential Privacy (DP) is being increasingly adopted for non-Euclidean data that lie on complex, high-dimensional manifolds. Existing DP mechanisms for manifold data consider geometric properties when calibrating privacy perturbations, but they largely fail to capture variations in data density within datasets, leading to biased perturbations and suboptimal privacy-utility trade-offs due to heterogeneous data distributions. In this paper, we propose a novel density-aware differential privacy mechanism on Riemannian manifolds, referred to as Conformal-DP, that leverages conformal transformations to calibrate perturbations based on local densities and to induce a density-balanced geometry. We prove that our mechanism satisfies $ε$-differential privacy on any complete Riemannian manifold under mild regularity assumptions. In addition, we derive a closed-form expected geodesic error bound that depends only on the underlying data density ratio and is independent of global curvature. Our empirical results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed Conformal-DP mechanism substantially improves the privacy-utility trade-off in heterogeneous data distribution settings, with worst-case performance comparable to state-of-the-art manifold DP mechanisms that assume uniformly distributed data.
papers.comments: Accepted on IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Scalable and adaptive prediction bands with kernel sum-of-squares
papers.abstract: Conformal Prediction (CP) is a popular framework for constructing prediction bands with valid coverage in finite samples, while being free of any distributional assumption. A well-known limitation of conformal prediction is the lack of adaptivity, although several works introduced practically efficient alternate procedures. In this work, we build upon recent ideas that rely on recasting the CP problem as a statistical learning problem, directly targeting coverage and adaptivity. This statistical learning problem is based on reproducible kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS) and kernel sum-of-squares (SoS) methods. First, we extend previous results with a general representer theorem and exhibit the dual formulation of the learning problem. Crucially, such dual formulation can be solved efficiently by accelerated gradient methods with several hundreds or thousands of samples, unlike previous strategies based on off-the-shelf semidefinite programming algorithms. Second, we introduce a new hyperparameter tuning strategy tailored specifically to target adaptivity through bounds on test-conditional coverage. This strategy, based on the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC), is introduced here to tune kernel lengthscales in our framework, but has broader applicability since it could be used in any CP algorithm where the score function is learned. Finally, extensive experiments are conducted to show how our method compares to related work. All figures can be reproduced with the accompanying code at \href{https://www.gitlab.com/drti/ksos-bands}{gitlab.com/drti/ksos-bands}.
papers.journal_ref: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025), Dec 2025, San Diego, United States

papers.title: New exact solutions of the 3D Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: Previously we found a unique quantum system with a positive gauge-invariant Weyl-Stratonovich quasi-probability density function which can be defined by the so-called «quadratic funnel» potential. In this work we have constructed a class of exact solutions to the 3D Schrödinger equation for a two-parameter «quadratic funnel» potential based on the $Ψ$ -model of micro and macro systems. It should be noted that the Aharonov-Bohm effect is inherent in the quantum $Ψ$ -model. Explicit expressions for the energy spectrum and the set of eigenfunctions have been found. Using gauge invariance for scalar and vector potentials, a solution to the electromagnetic Schrödinger equation has been obtained, with a magnetic field in the form of a «Dirac string» defined by a singular vortex probability flux field. Superpositions of eigenfunctions leading to various types of vortex and potential probability current fields have been investigated in detail. The analysis of the quantum system's properties has been carried out within the Wigner-Vlasov formalism.

papers.title: Unified Toolbox for Multipartite Entanglement Certification
papers.abstract: We present a unified framework for multipartite entanglement characterization based on the conditional gradient (CG) method, incorporating both fast heuristic detection and rigorous witness construction with numerical error control. Our method enables entanglement certification in quantum systems of up to ten qubits and applies to arbitrary entanglement structures. We demonstrate its power by closing the gap between entanglement and separability bounds in white-noise robustness benchmarks for a class of bound entangled states. Furthermore, the framework extends to entanglement robustness under general quantum noise channels, providing accurate thresholds in cases beyond the reach of previous algorithmic methods. These results position CG methods as a powerful tool for practical and scalable entanglement analysis in realistic experimental settings.
papers.comments: 6+10 pages, 12 figures; close to the published version

papers.title: Between Markov and restriction. Two more monads on categories for relations
papers.abstract: The study of categories abstracting the structural properties of relations has been extensively developed over the years, resulting in a rich and diverse body of work. In a previous paper we offered a survey providing a modern presentation of these ``categories for relations'' as instances of gs-monoidal categories, showing how they arise as Kleisli categories of suitable symmetric monoidal monads. The end result was a taxonomy that organised numerous related concepts in the literature, including in particular Markov and restriction categories. This paper further enriches the taxonomy: it proposes two categories that are once more instances of gs-monoidal categories, yet more abstract than Markov and restriction categories. They are characterised by an axiomatic notion of mass and domain of an arrow, the latter one of the key ingredients of restriction categories, which generalises the domain of partial functions. The paper then introduces mass and domain preserving monads, proving that the associated Kleisli categories in fact preserve the corresponding equations and that these monads arise naturally for the categories of semiring-weighted relations.

papers.title: How deep is your network? Deep vs. shallow learning of transfer operators
papers.abstract: We introduce RaNNDy, a randomized neural network framework for learning transfer operators and their spectral decompositions. By fixing the weights of the hidden layers and training only the output layer, RaNNDy achieves significant reductions in computational costs -- often by two orders of magnitude -- with similar accuracy compared to state-of-the-art deep learning methods. The method is less sensitive to hyperparameter tuning and provides a closed-form solution for the output layer weights that directly represent eigenfunctions of the learned operator. Moreover, it is possible to estimate uncertainties associated with the computed spectral properties via ensemble learning. We demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach using diverse benchmark problems, including stochastic dynamical systems and protein folding processes, highlighting the strengths but also weaknesses of RaNNDy.

papers.title: MAGDrop: Momentum Adaptive Gradient Dropout With Provable Generalization Guarantees
papers.abstract: Standard dropout applies a fixed, uniform noise rate to all units, ignoring available gradient information. We propose momentum adaptive gradient dropout (MAGDrop), a Bayesian linear layer that adapts per-unit weight noise by tracking an exponential moving average of gradient magnitudes. Units with large recent gradient magnitudes receive less noise to preserve learned features; units with below-average gradient magnitudes receive more noise to promote exploration. This adaptation transforms the classifier head into a data-dependent Bayesian predictor whose mean predictor has no additional inference cost. Our primary contribution is a certificate-aware low-rank posterior, MAGDrop-Subspace, that addresses the tension between strong accuracy and tight bounds from probably approximately correct (PAC)-Bayes theory. A full-head stochastic posterior incurs a Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence of approximately 8,625 nats. By confining the posterior to an $r$-dimensional subspace constructed from an independent prior-construction sample $S_0$ and certifying on an independent sample $S$ with $S_0\perp S$, MAGDrop-Subspace reduces KL by approximately a factor of 800 while keeping accuracy close to the baseline. On CIFAR-10 with a 13-layer convolutional neural network and $r=50$, MAGDrop-Subspace achieves a PAC-Bayes Gibbs-risk bound of 0.1882 at 90\% confidence using binary KL inversion, compared with 0.4439 for the full-head baseline. Mean-predictor accuracy is 82.31\%, compared with 83.74\% for the baseline. Complementary accuracy experiments on ImageNet-1K show that MAGDrop reaches top-1 accuracy similar to the strong baseline: 78.57\% compared with 78.51\% on the base Vision Transformer with $16\times16$ patches, and 82.14\% compared with 82.23\% on ConvNeXt-Base.
papers.comments: Revised version; submitted to IEEE TNNLS

papers.title: Recovering Geodesic Distances from Noisy Observations
papers.abstract: Let $(M,d,μ)$ be a nice geodesic probability space (such as a manifold) and $X=\{x_i\}_{i\in [N]} \subset M$ a finite $μ$-i.i.d. sample. Suppose we observe noisy distance random variables $d'(x_i,x_j)$. When can the true distances be recovered to small additive error? This question has attracted interest in two disparate fields: latent-space graph models and boundary-value inverse problems. We first show that, taking $N \asymp ε^{-2d-2}|\logε|$ and using runtime $O(N^{2.5+o_d (1)})$, we can recover all distances in $X$ to additive error $O(ε|\logε|)$ with high probability, assuming $\mathbb{E} d'(x_i, x_j) = F(d(x_i,x_j))$ for an unknown, increasing bilipschitz $F$ and with the $d'(x_i,x_j)$ allowed to be arbitrarily heterogeneous in their distribution as long as they are bounded in subgaussian norm. This generalizes existing work, which required $F$ to be known and made strict assumptions on the distribution of $d'(x_i, x_j)$. Achieving this generalization required a novel ``ruler-building'' procedure to learn $F$. We extend our results to a missing data case where we randomly lose access to noisy distances. Our second result uses ideas from the first to tackle a partial observability case: $X = Y \cup Z$ with $Z$ sampled from $M$ and $Y$ sampled from an observer subset satisfying visibility conditions that model the assumptions made on the boundary in boundary-value inverse problems. In this setting, we recover all pairwise distances in $Z$ to additive error $O(ε)$ with $|Z| \asymp ε^{-2d-2}|\logε|$, $|Y| \asymp ε^{-\max\{d_ν,4\}}$ with $d_ν$ determined by the volume-growth properties of the probability measure on the observer set, and runtime $O(|Z|^3)$. This is, to our knowledge, the first quantitative guarantee for this observer/observed split under noise, which complements existing stability results for boundary data.
papers.comments: 36 pages; a few added and modified results. Submitted to STOC 2027

papers.title: Exact Gaussian Moment Matching for Residual Networks: a Second-Order Method
papers.abstract: We study the problem of propagating the mean and covariance of a general multivariate Gaussian distribution through a deep (residual) neural network using layer-by-layer moment matching. We close a longstanding gap by deriving exact moment matching for the probit, GeLU, ReLU (as a limit of GeLU), Heaviside (as a limit of probit), and sine activation functions; for both feedforward and generalized residual layers. On large-variance random networks, median KL-divergence improvements over common baselines range from tens to thousands of times. On a variational Bayes neural network, we show that our method improves upon a state-of-the-art deterministic inference method by an order of magnitude in KL divergence from Monte Carlo ground truth. We also give a smooth-distance error bound showing that, under regularity assumptions, moment matching removes the leading low-variance errors and propagates higher-order local accuracy through the layers of a network.

papers.title: Accessing Levinson-Smith and Liénard equations in a nonlinear framework of quantum mechanics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present the reduction of a recently introduced generalized quantum scheme of Chodos and Cooper to Levinson-Smith and Liénard classes of nonlinear system that enable us to furnish a wider class of acceptable solutions. In particular, for the Levinson-Smith equations, we find their relevance to position-dependent mass quantum systems, with an interesting off-shoot that solitonic-like solutions emerge from the condition of the level surface in the system. On the other hand, for the Liénard type, which has coefficients of odd and odd symmetry in the present set up, we demonstrate that closed form solutions exist on carrying out conversion to the typical Abel form.
papers.comments: Title and text modified; references updated; 11 pages, 2 figures. Version accepted in Journal of Theoretical, Experimental, and Applied Physics

papers.title: GAP Measures and Wave Function Collapse
papers.abstract: GAP measures (also known as Scrooge measures) are a natural class of probability distributions on the unit sphere of a Hilbert space that come up in quantum statistical mechanics; for each density matrix $ρ$ there is a unique measure GAP$_ρ$. We describe and prove a property of these measures that was not recognized so far: If a wave function $Ψ$ is GAP$_ρ$ distributed and a collapse occurs, then the collapsed wave function $Ψ'$ is again GAP distributed (relative to the appropriate $ρ'$). This fact applies to collapses due to a quantum measurement carried out by an observer, as well as to spontaneous collapse theories such as CSL or GRW. More precisely, it is the conditional distribution of $Ψ'$, given the measurement outcome (respectively, the noise in CSL or the collapse history in GRW), that is GAP$_{ρ'}$.
papers.comments: 12 pages LaTeX, no figures; changes in v2: Section 4 added and minor corrections and improvements throughout the paper

papers.title: On the non-uniformity of the 2026 FIFA World Cup draw
papers.abstract: The group stage of a sports tournament is often made more appealing by introducing additional constraints in the group draw that promote an attractive and balanced group composition. For example, the number of intra-regional group matches is minimised in several world championships. Under such constraints, the traditional draw procedure may become non-uniform, meaning that the feasible allocations of the teams into groups are not equally likely to occur. Our paper quantifies this non-uniformity of the 2026 FIFA World Cup draw for the official draw procedure, as well as for 47 reasonable alternatives implied by all permutations of the four pots and two group labelling policies. We show why simulating with a recursive backtracking algorithm is intractable, and propose a workable implementation using integer programming. The official draw mechanism is found to be optimal based on two of five non-uniformity measures, including the average distortion of the 771 non-zero assignment probabilities. Nonetheless, non-uniformity can be more than halved if the organiser aims to treat the best teams drawn from the first pot equally.

papers.title: Complete Diagrammatic Axiomatisations of Relative Entropy
papers.abstract: Relative entropy is a fundamental class of distances between probability distributions, with widespread applications in probability theory, statistics, and machine learning. In this work, we study relative entropy from a categorical perspective, viewing it as a quantitative enrichment of categories of stochastic matrices. We consider two natural monoidal structures on stochastic matrices, given by the Kronecker product and the direct sum. Our main results are complete axiomatisations of Kullback-Leibler divergence and, more generally, of Rényi divergences of arbitrary order, for each such structure. Our axiomatic theories are formulated within the framework of quantitative monoidal algebra, using a graphical language of string diagrams enriched with quantitative equations.
papers.comments: Final proceedings version for MFPS XLII

papers.title: The $\mathrm{al}_{ab}$ functions of hyperelliptic curves: a generalization of Jacobi's elliptic functions and explicit solutions of a degenerate Krichever-Novikov equation
papers.abstract: The Jacobi elliptic functions $\mathrm{sn}$, $\mathrm{cn}$, $\mathrm{dn}$ and their ratios are expressed by Weierstrass's functions $\mathrm{al}_a=\sqrt{x-b_a}$ of an elliptic curve. For a hyperelliptic curve of genus $g$, Weierstrass's $\mathrm{al}_a$ functions generalize $\mathrm{sn}$, $\mathrm{cn}$ and $\mathrm{dn}$, and the modified Korteweg-de Vries and sine-Gordon equations stand behind them. In this paper we study the $\mathrm{al}_{ab}$ functions, which are defined by the sigma function shifted by the sum of two half-periods and which, together with the ratios of the $\mathrm{al}_a$ functions, generalize the remaining Jacobi elliptic functions. We determine the exact lattice of periods of $\mathrm{al}_{12}$ and show that it is single-valued on the unramified double covering of the Jacobian corresponding to the double covering $\hat{w}^2=(x-b_1)(x-b_2)$ of the curve. We show that $\mathrm{al}_{12}$ is the Wronskian of the band-edge eigenfunctions $\mathrm{al}_1$ and $\mathrm{al}_2$, so that the half-period translations realize Darboux transformations. As the main result, $\mathrm{al}_{12}$, $\mathrm{al}_2/\mathrm{al}_1$ and $1/\mathrm{al}_{12}$ satisfy one and the same degenerate Krichever-Novikov equation, whose polynomial has the double roots $0$ and $\infty$, and the half-periods act on these solutions as the Möbius symmetries of the equation. Thus the Krichever-Novikov equation stands behind the $\mathrm{al}_{ab}$ functions. In genus one these functions reduce to $\mathrm{sn}$, $\mathrm{ns}$ and $\mathrm{dc}$.

papers.title: Quantum Dynamical Entropy and non-Markovianity: a collisional model perspective
papers.abstract: Accessing the physical mechanisms behind non-Markovian phenomena in open quantum dynamics requires the study of the statistical properties of the joint system-environment dynamics. This is impossible at the level of the reduced dynamics of the open system alone as the latter is obtained by suitably eliminating the environment. The task is instead made possible by considering multi-time correlation functions involving observables of the open system, only: the open system-environment interactions turn them into global ones thus building up correlations between the two systems. Multi-time correlations form the basis of both the theory of quantum stochastic processes and of the Alicki-Lindblad-Fannes dynamical entropy (ALF entropy for short). This latter quantity provides for quantum systems a measure of the dynamical entropy production as the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy does for classical systems. In the case of a collisional model whereby the dissipative dynamics of a finite-level system is obtained by its coupling to an infinite classical spin chain, the ALF entropy can be explicitly computed. It turns out to depend on the parameters characterizing the statistical properties of the environment and can be related to the activation and super-activation of memory effects in the open quantum system.
papers.comments: 31 pages, 3 figures; revised and expanded version. See also the companion Letter arXiv:2603.14025

papers.title: Quantum Dynamical Entropy and Dissipative Information Flows
papers.abstract: The Alicki-Lindblad-Fannes dynamical (ALF) entropy measures the rate at which new information is gathered about a quantum system by inspecting its long-time evolution. We propose an extension of the ALF entropy to open quantum dynamics as a measure of back-flow of information from the environment. Such a proposal is stronger than the existing ones based only on the open system reduced dynamics. In the case of a qubit collisionally coupled to a classical spin chain, we obtain an exact expression for the $\textit{open-system ALF entropy}$ explicitly depending on the environment correlations. An extreme case shows how the information flow from environment to system corresponds to vanishing entropy production as for reversible finite quantum systems.
papers.comments: 6 pages, 2 figures; see also the companion paper arXiv:2603.14015

papers.title: Convex algebras on an interval with semicontinuous monotone operations
papers.abstract: In a recent work of Matteo Mio on compact quantitative equational theories (here compact means that all its consequences are derivable by means of finite proofs) convex algebras on the carrier set [0,1] whose operations are monotone and satisfy certain semicontinuity properties occurred. We fully classify those algebraic structures by giving an explicit construction of all possible convex operations on [0,1] possessing the mentioned properties. Our result thus describes exactly the range of theories to which Mio's theorem applies.

papers.title: On the average-case complexity landscape for Tensor-Isomorphism-complete problems over finite fields
papers.abstract: In Grochow and Qiao (\emph{SIAM J. Comput.}, 2023), the complexity class Tensor Isomorphism (TI) was introduced and isomorphism problems for groups, algebras, and polynomials were shown to be TI-complete. In this paper, we study average-case algorithms for several TI-complete problems over finite fields, including algebra isomorphism, matrix code conjugacy, and $4$-tensor isomorphism. Our main results reveal a rich landscape of average-case complexities of Tensor Isomorphism problems, despite their equivalence in the worst-case setting. Over the finite field of order $q$, we devise (1) average-case \emph{polynomial-time} algorithms for algebra isomorphism and matrix code conjugacy that succeed for $1/Θ(q)$ fraction of inputs; (2) an average-case \emph{polynomial-time} algorithm for the $4$-tensor isomorphism that succeeds for $1/q^{Θ(1)}$ fraction of inputs; and (3) an average-case \emph{polynomial-time} algorithm for the orthogonal $3$-tensor isomorphism that succeed for $1-1/\poly(n)$ fraction of $n\times n\times n$ tensors. Our main technical contribution is to introduce the spectral properties of random matrices into algorithms for TI-complete problems. This leads to not only new algorithms but also new questions in random matrix theory over finite fields. To settle these questions, we need to extend both the generating function approach as in Neumann and Praeger (\emph{J. London Math. Soc.}, 1998) and the character sum method of Gorodetsky and Rodgers (\emph{Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.}, 2021).
papers.comments: 60 pages, add average-case polynomial-time algorithm for orthogonal tensor isomorphism over finite field

papers.title: Univalence without function extensionality
papers.abstract: It is a well-known theorem of homotopy type theory, originally due to Voevodsky, that function extensionality holds inside any univalent universe. We consider a weaker variant of the univalence axiom, asserting that the wild category formed by the universe is univalent, which we call categorical univalence. We show that categorical univalence does not imply function extensionality by an analysis of Von Glehn's polynomial model construction, which produces models of Martin-Löf type theory that always refute function extensionality. We find in particular that when the base model has a univalent universe, its polynomial model has a universe that is categorically univalent but lacks function extensionality.

papers.title: Optimal Zonotope Containment via Adaptive Gaussian Sampling
papers.abstract: We investigate the convex-body containment problem $\max\{s >0 : s Z \subseteq Q\}$, where the outer body $Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is described by a membership oracle and the inner body $Z \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is a zonotope. Our main result is a sampling-based $O(\sqrt{d/\log d})$-approximation algorithm for this problem that matches the lower bound of $Ω(\sqrt{d/\log d})$ by Khot and Naor in the oracle model. Starting from approximate Lewis position, the algorithm samples Gaussian directions and adaptively shortens and repositions the generators. Its analysis combines preservation of the support in a fixed direction with contraction of the corresponding functional after renormalization. Crucially, the algorithm works directly with the input generators and does not use zonotope sparsification. We complement this result with a \emph{universal} $Ω(\sqrt{d/\log d})$ lower bound holding for \emph{all} full-dimensional zonotopes when the number of oracle queries is polynomial in $d$. Finally, we consider containment problems $\max\{s >0 : s K \subseteq Q\}$, for general convex bodies $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$. A result of Nasz{ó}di on approximating $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ by a polytope implies a $Θ(d/\log d)$ approximation algorithm in polynomial time when the centroid of $K$ is the origin. We show the tightness of this approximation factor in the oracle model via a reduction to the circumradius computation. Our lower bound holds for centrally symmetric convex sets, implying that Barvinok's optimal $O(\sqrt{d})$-approximation of a centrally symmetric convex body by a polytope with a polynomial number of vertices cannot be computed in polynomial time.

papers.title: Almost Sure Convergence Rates of Stochastic Approximation and Reinforcement Learning via a Poisson-Moreau Drift
papers.abstract: Establishing almost sure convergence rates for stochastic approximation and reinforcement learning under Markovian noise is a fundamental theoretical challenge. We make progress towards this challenge for a class of stochastic approximation algorithms whose expected updates are contractive, a setting that arises in many reinforcement learning algorithms such as $Q$-learning and linear temporal difference learning. Specifically, for a power-law learning rate $O(n^{-η})$ with $η\in (1/2, 1)$, we obtain an almost sure convergence rate arbitrarily close to $o(n^{1 - 2η})$. For the harmonic learning rate $α_n=α/(n+1)$, the almost sure squared-error rate is $o(n^{-ζ})$ for every $ζ<\min\{1,2(1-κ)α\}$, where $κ$ is the contraction factor. Thus exponents arbitrarily close to one are available when $2(1-κ)α\geq1$. This approaches the $n^{-1}$ polynomial exponent of classical law-of-the-iterated-logarithm benchmarks. Key to our analysis is a novel Lyapunov drift construction that applies a Poisson-equation based correction for Markovian noise to the well-established Moreau-envelope smoothing for the contractive mapping.

papers.title: Scaling Limits of Long-Context Transformers
papers.abstract: We study the long-context limit of softmax self-attention with a fixed query and a random context of $n$ i.i.d. keys on the sphere with the intrinsic dimension of the key distribution held fixed, viewing the inverse temperature $β_n$ as the scaling parameter that decides whether attention degenerates into uniform averaging or collapses onto the single closest key. We show that the critical scale at which selectivity emerges is determined by the local exponent of the distance-to-query distribution near zero rather than by global features of the context, and scales like $β_n^\ast \asymp n^{2/(d-1)}$ for uniform keys on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$. Furthermore, we characterize the limiting laws of the ordered attention weights and of the attention output across all regimes of $β_n$: a subcritical regime in which the output reduces to a local average around $q$ with explicit deterministic bias and Gaussian fluctuations; a critical regime in which a finite collection of nearest keys retains macroscopic mass without single-key collapse; and a supercritical regime in which all mass concentrates on the closest key. Of notable interest is the subcritical case with identity value matrix where the attention map approximately implements a backward heat equation.

papers.title: The Symmetric Location Problem: a Song of Efficiency and Robustness
papers.abstract: The aim of this Lecture Note is to introduce the Signal Processing (SP) community to a powerful yet still under-utilised tool: the semiparametric statistics. In short, the semiparametric framework allows us to estimate or perform hypothesis testing on a finite-dimensional parameter $\boldsymbolθ \in Θ\subseteq \mathbb{R}^p$ in the presence of an \textit{infinite-dimensional nuisance parameter} $g \in \mathcal{S}$ (i.e. a function), such as the density of the noise. Clearly, this framework is general enough to include almost every SP application. Remarkably, as the title suggests drawing on George R. R. Martin's famous book series, the greatest advantage of semiparametric statistics over parametric and non-parametric ones lies in the fact that it is able to reconcile two seemingly dichotomous concepts: statistical efficiency and distributional robustness. To explain exactly what this means, in this Lecture Note we will focus our attention on the famous and fundamental symmetric location problem.

papers.title: Eigenvalue formulation of Stochastic Inflation and application to large perturbation generating inflationary features
papers.abstract: Stochastic inflation is a powerful technique for calculating the probability distribution function (PDF) of large inflationary perturbations, which may collapse to form Primordial Black Holes. The PDF, $P({\cal N})$, of the stochastic number of e-folds, ${\cal N}$, satisfies an adjoint Fokker-Planck Equation. We develop a new self-contained eigenvalue technique which can be used to determine $P({\cal N})$. First we apply this method to the simple case of quantum diffusion along a flat potential without any classical drift. We recover the expression for the PDF that has previously been found using characteristic functions, with an exponential tail, and a power-law behaviour, $P({\cal N}) \propto {\cal N}^{-3/2}$, in the intermediate regime between the peak and the tail of the PDF. Finally we apply the method to constant drift inflation, in the narrow- and broad-well limits. In the narrow-well limit, there is an analytic solution and the PDF is similar to the drift-free case, with a mildly suppressed tail. In the broad-well limit, determining the full set of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions requires a piecewise construction of the spectrum, and the broad-well PDF is qualitatively different, with an enhanced peak and a strongly suppressed tail.
papers.comments: 40 pages, 11 figures, minor text revisions; matches the accepted version in JCAP

papers.title: How Deep Are Deep GPs, Really? A Sharp Threshold and a Non-Gaussian Limit for Compositional GPs
papers.abstract: Compositional priors describe the generic properties of layered functions in deep Bayesian models, where deep neural networks with random weights are a canonical example. In the wide-network limit, the prior is a Gaussian process (GP) with a depth-dependent kernel, and its behaviour as depth grows has been extensively studied through this kernel. Here, we study another case, where each layer itself is a vector valued Gaussian process, and our aim is similarly to understand the limiting behaviour of the prior as depth grows. Previous GP work has established that for the radial basis function (RBF) kernel and a certain range of bandwidths $r$, the prior degenerates in the limit, converging to the set of constant functions, which is not useful as a probabilistic model. In this paper we establish several new results. First, we identify a sharp bandwidth threshold $r_c(d) = Θ(\sqrt{d})$ above which the limit is degenerate, strengthening the earlier bounds. Second, and more importantly, we show that for $r$ below the threshold $r_c(d)$ the prior converges to a limit distribution $π_{\bar{Z}}$. We also prove that these distributions are non-degenerate and non-Gaussian, with non-vanishing dependence between coordinates. In contrast to the previously known degenerate regime, deep Gaussian process priors can therefore admit non-trivial limits. Empirically, we verify the threshold across a range of dimensions $d$, and demonstrate a complex multimodal behaviour of the limit distributions $π_{\bar{Z}}$, a regime that becomes increasingly narrow with $d$ and would be hard to identify without knowing the threshold.

papers.title: Isotropic random walks and Brownian diffusion on complex projective space
papers.abstract: We study isotropic random walks on complex projective space in the context of stochastic state-space exploration in open quantum systems. Using results from harmonic analysis on compact rank-one symmetric spaces, first we obtain explicit transition kernels and characterise the evolution of fidelity and geometric observables. Then, we establish the correspondence between the small-step limit and Fubini-Study Brownian motion, and also show that the long-time limit reproduces Haar-random state statistics. At the level of the density matrix, the ensemble evolution formally coincides with an isotropic depolarizing channel at all times. Our main results concern first-passage statistics to high-fidelity target states. In the Brownian limit, we derive a closed-form expression for the mean first-passage time and an explicit spectral representation of the first-passage-time distribution, with decay rates determined by the eigenvalues of the killed Fubini-Study Laplace-Beltrami operator. The resulting asymptotics reveal a strong dependence on target fidelity and Hilbert-space dimension, demonstrating the rapidly increasing difficulty of reaching high-fidelity targets through unbiased isotropic exploration. The model is purely geometric and does not incorporate microscopic Hamiltonians or Lindblad dynamics. Nevertheless, the results suggest that it offers a natural starting point for stochastic models of open quantum systems that incorporate Hamiltonian and dissipative effects, with potential applications to stochastic quantum state preparation and control.

papers.title: Symbol sequences from three-rotor coincidences and their word-complexity
papers.abstract: In the three-rotor problem, three equally massive point particles move on a circle interacting via attractive pairwise cosine potentials. Rotors can represent superconducting phases of metallic segments in a chain of coupled Josephson junctions. We propose a digitization of the classical dynamics that records successive pair and triple coincidences of rotors using four symbols. Rotor coincidences correspond to boundaries in a disjoint partition of the configuration torus into cells where the rotors are ordered clockwise and anticlockwise. It is shown that isolated rotor coincidences must be crossings. Despite being a rather coarse digitization, we find that replacing trajectories by coincidence symbol sequences captures significant qualitative features of the dynamics through word statistics. Word-complexity $C_n$ measures the diversity of $n$-letter words in the symbol sequence while topological entropy governs asymptotic exponential growth of $C_n$. Sequences from periodic orbits have a word-complexity that saturates at the period. Ultra-high-energy trajectories with irrational `slope' are quasiperiodic. We show that they have zero entropy and $C_n = n+3$ by examining limiting slopes and by a mapping to Sturmian sequences. We examine their grammar rules and propose how their right-special words may be identified. On the other hand, numerical investigation of sequences from globally chaotic orbits leads us to conjecture an exponentially growing word-complexity $C_n = 3 \times 2^{n-1}$ with a topological entropy $\log 2$. We identify grammar rules that imply this conjectured word-complexity and model the resulting sequences as a subshift of finite type, unlike those at ultra-high energies which are not topological Markov chains.

papers.title: A Single Physical Principle Determines Quantum Relative Entropy
papers.abstract: Why does quantum relative entropy occupy such a privileged role among measures of distinguishability? We show that a single operational principle determines it. If one pair of states can be distinguished at least as successfully as another for every prior, when both are assisted by the same auxiliary pair, acting as a catalyst, a distinguishability measure should assign it no smaller value. Remarkably, for a normalized measure, this requirement singles out Umegaki relative entropy under mild classical continuity and expansibility on uniform distributions: adding impossible outcomes leaves their associated entropy unchanged. Qubit catalysts already suffice. No additivity or quantum continuity is assumed. We also prove that, without auxiliary assistance, respecting binary discrimination dominance uniquely determines the quantum extension of every regular classical divergence, including the Hirche--Tomamichel extensions of classical $f$-divergences. For additive classical divergences, these extensions respect classical catalysis; allowing noncommuting qubit catalysts is what singles out Umegaki relative entropy.
papers.comments: Major revision with a substantially stronger uniqueness theorem: catalytic Lorenz monotonicity characterizes Umegaki relative entropy without assuming additivity; full-rank qubit catalysts suffice. Includes a new proof and results distinguishing classical from quantum catalysis

papers.title: Symmetries and Conservation Laws in Lie-Poisson Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: Lie-Poisson electrodynamics (LPE) is a non-Abelian and nonlinear deformation of usual electrodynamics, where the gauge algebra is defined through a Lie-algebra-type Poisson bracket on space-time. This field-theoretical model arises from noncommutative U(1) gauge theory in the semiclassical limit. We focus on the geometric approach to LPE in the absence of charged matter. We establish a non-trivial field redefinition which, under mild technical assumptions, maps the LPE dynamics to that of Maxwell theory. We emphasise that despite the dynamical equivalence, these two theories are not physically equivalent, since the corresponding local gauge-invariant observables are different. We show that our field redefinition is actually a Seiberg-Witten map between LPE and Maxwell theory. Using this map, for any symmetry of the Maxwell action, we construct generators of LPE symmetries and the corresponding conserved currents. In particular, we obtain deformed Poincaré transformations, thereby solving the problem of constructing space-time symmetries in LPE. The deformed symmetries are constructed as active transformations of the gauge field. In the outlook, we propose a natural quantization prescription for LPE based on our field redefinition.
papers.comments: extended version, references added, 19 pages; to appear in Nucl. Phys. B

papers.title: Optimizing the Preconditioner: A Black-box Online-to-Nonconvex Conversion with Static Regret Minimization Oracles
papers.abstract: Stochastic nonconvex optimization is central to training deep networks and LLMs in modern machine learning. We give a black-box reduction from stochastic nonconvex optimization to ordinary static regret minimization in online convex optimization (OCO), addressing the open problem posed by Chen and Hazan (2024). Our reduction maintains a predictable gradient tracker, while a black-box online learner $\mathcal A$ selects a preconditioner that transforms this tracker into the update direction. Given a $β$-smooth function with initial gap at most $M$ and an unbiased gradient oracle with variance bounded by $σ^2$, we bound the expected average squared gradient norm by $O(σ\sqrt{Mβ/T}+\sqrt{Mβ}\mathrm{Reg}_T(\mathcal A)/T+\frac{Mβ}{T})$, where $\mathrm{Reg}_T(\mathcal A)$ is the static regret of $\mathcal A$ against the identity preconditioner. Thus, any OCO oracle with $O(\sqrt T)$ regret recovers the classical $O(T^{-1/2})$ convergence rate. We also prove that the additive variance term cannot be removed: every conversion making a constant number of stochastic-oracle queries per round, whose guarantee is stated through static regret against a comparator that the online learner can play, must contain an additive term of order $σ\sqrt{Mβ/T}$ for sufficiently large $T$. Moreover, for every online learner, our conversion bound is tight up to universal constants. We also extend the framework to nonsmooth nonconvex optimization, still relying only on ordinary static regret, and attain the optimal convergence rate for Goldstein-type stationarity. Finally, we conduct numerical experiments on nonconvex objectives to illustrate how the reduction exploits online-selected preconditioners while using the same stochastic-oracle budget as stochastic gradient descent.

papers.title: Relativistic transport near moving interfaces
papers.abstract: We study linear disturbances localized near planar surfaces moving at constant velocity $v$ in relativistic media. Depending on the physical setting, the surface may represent a moving obstacle, a thermal boundary, or an external source, providing a unified description of boundary layers, wakes, and the asymptotic tails of shock waves. The central result is a propagator representation of the interface solution that yields a geometric characterization of these phenomena. Using a Laplace-transform formulation, we show that the solution is a superposition of modes with purely imaginary frequency and wavenumber. For a given interface velocity, the admissible modes are selected by the line $iω=vik$ in the $\{iω,ik\}$ plane. As $v$ varies, this line sweeps across the spectrum, providing a unified geometric description of interface-localized solutions for arbitrary interface velocities. We illustrate the formalism with applications to relativistic hydrodynamics and kinetic theory.

papers.title: Topological Computational Paths: Presentation Invariance and Observable Quotients
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz
papers.abstract: A computational path records the steps used to establish an equality. Topologies on computational equality witnesses can depend on the chosen generators and execution schedule, even when their algebraic and homotopical meanings agree. We study continuous presentations of finite computational paths whose declared rewrites are realized by endpoint-fixed homotopies. We compare a topology retaining the full signed trace with an observable topology recording endpoints, length, and exact path realization. Continuous finite-word interpretations that are inverse up to scoped rewriting preserve trace-sensitive quotient arrows and their final composable-pair spaces. Observable quotients behave differently. Over a point with a nonempty primitive alphabet, we classify their topology: it records length parity when all named relations preserve parity, and is otherwise indiscrete. Adjoining a conservative abbreviation can therefore turn a discrete two-element quotient into an indiscrete space, even though ordinary multiplication remains continuous. A circle presentation also gives nonhomeomorphic quotients under binary and equal-slot timing. Geometric completeness alone does not identify the trace-sensitive and observable topologies. Multiplication is continuous on the quotient of composable representatives. We characterize when this topology agrees with the ordinary pullback topology and give an open-projection criterion. Universal presentations recover classical fundamental-groupoid topology. Normal forms, primitive interchange, and a Cayley covering prove completeness for circle, torus, product, and rose presentations. A literal-word correspondence relates the semantics to the reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity fragment of equality derivations. Selected results are formalized in Lean, with the realization models and proof coverage stated explicitly.
papers.comments: 34 pages, 10 figures. Substantially revised and retitled; expanded presentation-invariance results, observable-quotient counterexamples, and geometric completeness examples; clarified formalization scope. Lean artifact: https://github.com/Arthur742Ramos/TopologicalComputationalPaths

papers.title: Rigorous Low-Degree Implications for Planted Subgraph Detection: Noise and Treewidth
papers.abstract: The low-degree method predicts computational thresholds by asking whether low-degree polynomials can distinguish a planted distribution from a null one. Recent counterexamples by Buhai, Hsieh, Jain, and Kothari (FOCS 2025) and Mao (2026) show that low-degree indistinguishability does not, in general, rule out efficient algorithms, even on noisy inputs. Hsieh, Kane, Kothari, Li, Mohanty, and Tiegel (STOC 2026) asked what it does imply, and showed that for permutation-invariant distributions on $\{0,1\}^n$, low-degree indistinguishability from the uniform distribution implies statistical indistinguishability after noise. In this work, we study the same question for planted subgraphs in sparse random graphs. Let $Q_n=G(n,c/n)$, and let $P_n$ be obtained by planting a uniformly random copy of a deterministic graph $Γ_n$ into an independent sample from $Q_n$. In the supercritical regime $c>1$, we show that if $P_n$ is degree-$D_n$ indistinguishable from $Q_n$ and the treewidth of $Γ_n$ is $o(D_n/\log n)$, then a noisy version of $P_n$ is asymptotically indistinguishable from $Q_n$. In the critical and subcritical regimes $0<c\le 1$, we obtain the same conclusion without any treewidth assumption, provided $D_n=ω(\log n)$. Our proof has two main ingredients. First, we identify the subgraph-count and automorphism factors in the Fourier expansion with counts of isomorphism triples. Second, we cut a tree decomposition of $Γ_n$ into subtrees, which splits each large Fourier support into low-degree pieces that meet at only a few interface vertices, and we use noise to absorb the cost of reassembling them. At and below criticality, we use the low-degree assumption to rule out short cycles and noise to destroy the remaining long ones.

papers.title: A Spectral Local-to-Global Principle for Spin Systems on Graphs with Girth At Least Five
papers.abstract: It is proved that, for every $δ\in (0,1)$, the Glauber dynamics for the uniform distribution on proper $q$-colorings is rapidly mixing when $q \geq (1+δ)Δ$ and the underlying graph has girth at least $5$ and maximum degree $Δ= Ω_δ(1)$. This result also extends to general multi-spin systems satisfying a $\textit{local spectral contraction}$ condition, including the anti-ferromagnetic Potts model with $q\geq (1+δ)(1-β)Δ$. These results are achieved by a new spectral local-to-global principle on graphs with girth at least five for general multi-spin systems, and a novel Fourier analysis for Glauber dynamics on a star. The main ideas behind all the proofs were developed through several rounds of interaction with GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra.

papers.title: Quadratic Complexity of Voronoi Diagrams in $\mathbb{R}^3$ for Lines in a Single Ruling of a Regulus
papers.abstract: We study nearest and farthest Voronoi diagrams of lines in three-dimensional Euclidean space, which partition space according to the closest and farthest input lines, respectively. For arbitrary lines, a gap remains between the known quadratic lower bound and near-cubic upper bounds for the complexity of the nearest diagram. We consider input lines chosen from one of two continuous families of straight lines on a smooth surface defined by a quadratic equation, with one line from each family passing through every point of the surface. Under the geometric assumptions stated in the paper, we prove quadratic upper bounds on the total number of vertices, edges, faces, and connected three-dimensional regions in both diagrams. We also construct quadratically many nearest vertices using lines from a single family on one fixed surface, establishing a tight quadratic worst-case bound. The farthest diagram has quadratic total complexity for every input satisfying our assumptions. Our proof uses a parametrization that arranges the input lines in a cyclic order and expresses tangency to a sphere by a polynomial equation of degree four. At a Voronoi vertex, the four tangent input lines give four distinct roots. The sign changes between these roots, together with the nearest or farthest condition, force two intervening parameter intervals to contain no other input parameters. Thus, only quadratically many choices of four lines can define a vertex, and each choice yields at most eight isolated candidate centers.
papers.comments: Added a coauthor, more detailed explanations of algebraic geometry, and additional figures

papers.title: Sparse Koopman Autoencoders Identify Local Dynamical Regimes in Multibasin Systems
papers.abstract: Koopman autoencoders (KAEs) seek a higher-dimensional latent representation in which nonlinear dynamics evolve linearly. However, many interesting systems have multiple basins of attraction, and both theoretical and empirical work has shown these multibasin systems cannot generally admit a single finite-dimensional global Koopman embedding under standard assumptions. We posit that encoders with a sparsity-inducing objective encouraging few active latent coefficients will provide latent supports as an inspectable basin-modeling principle for Koopman autoencoders. We use these encoders producing sparse latents in training Sparse Koopman Autoencoders (SKAEs) without basin labels or other regime annotations, and treat the learned latent supports as model-produced regime variables after training. Across a range of procedurally generated multibasin systems and chaotic flows, we show that SKAEs have superior forecasting performance compared to dense-latent KAEs. We also perform a mechanistic study that shows latent supports produced by SKAEs are both essential for the quality of the representation and useful for identifying basins on basin-interior states, whereas dense-latent KAEs collapse to an uninformative single support family. These results identify sparse latents and their corresponding supports as label-free, interpretable regime variables for Koopman learning in nonlinear systems with multiple local dynamical laws.
papers.comments: v3: changed code url. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 33 pages (10 pages main text) including references and appendices, 6 figures

papers.title: Max Independent Set Remains NP-hard when Excluding a Planar Induced Minor (and More)
papers.abstract: We show that Max Independent Set (MIS) remains NP-hard in graphs excluding the $5 \times 5$ grid as an induced minor. This negatively answers a question of Dallard--Milanič--Štorgel that has attracted sustained attention, and refutes a conjecture by Gartland and Lokshtanov. Unless $N$-variable 3-SAT can be solved in time $2^{\mathcal O(N^{1-\varepsilon})}$ for some $\varepsilon > 0$, MIS requires $2^{Ω(n^{1/2-o(1)})}$ time on $n$-vertex graphs in this class. This complements a $2^{\widetilde{O}(n^{2/3})}$-time algorithm on any $H$-induced-minor-free class by Korhonen and Lokshtanov. Exploiting a connection between low twin-width or reduced parameters on one hand and planar-induced-minor-freeness on the other, we further show that 3-Coloring, Feedback Vertex Set and Dominating Set are NP-complete on weakly sparse graphs of reduced component max-leaf (hence twin-width) at most 3, even when a witnessing contraction sequence is given. Classes of bounded reduced component max-leaf (by any constant) and of twin-width at most 3 are known to exclude a fixed planar graph as an induced minor. The 3-Coloring and Feedback Vertex Set results refute more cases of the Gartland--Lokshtanov conjecture, even when the inputs are weakly sparse. The complexity of MIS in weakly sparse graphs excluding a planar induced minor remains open.

papers.title: Polynomial-time Tensor Decomposition under the Kruskal Condition and the Lovitz--Petrov Generalization
papers.abstract: An identifiability criterion is a condition on a tensor decomposition that certifies uniqueness when the condition holds. Kruskal's classical condition is one of the best-known deterministic criteria for identifiability. However, no polynomial-time decomposition algorithm is known under the Kruskal condition; verifying the condition itself is NP-hard. Lovitz and Petrov introduced a strictly more general identifiability condition which, in contrast, is polynomial-time verifiable, but no polynomial-time decomposition algorithm was known under this condition either. In this paper we give a randomized polynomial-time algorithm, in the algebraic model over $\mathbb R$, for tensor decomposition under the Lovitz--Petrov condition, and therefore also under the stricter Kruskal condition. Moreover, combining our algorithm with polynomial-time verification of the Lovitz--Petrov condition yields an efficient end-to-end certification procedure: after computing a decomposition, one can deterministically certify in polynomial time that it is unique and therefore of minimum rank.

papers.title: Kadison--Singer in Deterministic Polynomial Time
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given rational Hermitian matrices $H_1,\dots,H_N$ of rank at most one, finds signs $s\in\{\pm1\}^N$ with $\|\sum_i s_i H_i\|\le 13\|\sum_i H_i^2\|^{1/2}$. As a corollary, for vectors $v_i$ with $\sum_i v_iv_i^*=I$ and $\|v_i\|^2\leδ$, the signs yield a partition $[N] = S_1 \cup S_2$ such that each part satisfies $\|\sum_{i \in S_j} v_i v_i^* - \frac{I}{2}\| \leq \frac{13}{2}\sqrtδ$ for $j = 1,2$. This gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the Kadison--Singer problem, in Weaver's equivalent discrepancy-theoretic $\mathsf{KS}_2$ formulation, with a universal constant.

papers.title: A Square-Root Barrier to Quantum Gate Speed under Linear Coupling
papers.abstract: Faster quantum gates can reduce the decoherence accumulated during a computation, but in superconducting processors, speeding up gates often involves stronger microwave pulses, which can increase leakage, off-resonant excitation, stray-field errors, and crosstalk. This creates a central energy--speed--error tradeoff: can quantum state engineering make a gate faster without paying proportionally more drive energy? We address this question by treating the driving pulse as a quantum bosonic field rather than a classical waveform. For a finite-dimensional system coupled linearly to that field, we prove that gate transition rates at fixed trace distance between the initial and final system states grow at most as the square root of the pulse energy, under pulse-uniformity conditions, without assuming an upper bound on the coupling strength. The bound permits arbitrary pulse states, including squeezed and non-Gaussian states, as well as drive--system entanglement and back action; coherent Gaussian pulses attain its energy exponent. Thus squeezing or other state engineering alone cannot replace the square-root energy law of a conventional linear drive by the linear scaling allowed by general quantum speed limits. Achieving that improvement requires changing the interaction class, in addition to using a suitable nonclassical pulse, thereby identifying interaction nonlinearity as an essential resource for relaxing the practical gate-speed error tradeoff.
papers.comments: Proves same bounds but under much weaker assumptions. Added operational interpretation of physical assumptions. 5 + 36 pages

papers.title: Vector Balancing in Polynomial Time
papers.abstract: The Komlós problem asks for signs $\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}^n$ with $\|A\varepsilon\|_\infty$ bounded by an absolute constant whenever the columns of $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ have Euclidean norm at most $1$. We give the first polynomial-time algorithm for this problem in the unit-cost real-RAM model. Our deterministic algorithm achieves discrepancy at most $8272$. As a consequence, we obtain a deterministic $O(\sqrt t)$-discrepancy algorithm for the Beck-Fiala problem on set systems in which each element belongs to at most $t$ sets. Our algorithm rounds a fractional coloring while keeping the row sums bounded. Its key idea is to keep the number of nearly tight row constraints small relative to the number of active coordinates. We achieve this through a spectral bound based on a weighted Gram matrix of squared row entries. We maintain the bound using a cubic spectral potential and negative-curvature updates that satisfy the required linear constraints.

papers.title: Bayesian Optimization with Fisher Information Geometry: Gradient Bounds and Trust-Region Methods
papers.abstract: We study Bayesian optimization (BO) through the lens of information geometry. Pulling back the Fisher information metric through the surrogate posterior map yields a local sensitivity tensor on the input space, which leads to an upper bound on the gradient of reparameterizable acquisition functions (AFs). This view explains vanishing-gradient behavior in high-dimensional BO and provides a common interpretation of heuristics such as RAASP and dimension-scaled lengthscales. The upper bound can also serve as a generic recipe to understand the behavior of new acquisition functions or surrogates in high input dimensions as well. Using the bounds, we also identify necessary conditions for an input location to be an optimizer of the AF for a univariate Gaussian predictive posterior. Building on this analysis, we propose FITR, a trust-region-based BO method that replaces lengthscale-based scaling with local pullback-Fisher weights. FITR is not restricted to GP kernels with explicit lengthscales and easily generalizes to non-isotropic surrogates. FITR shows competitive performance on several benchmarks.

papers.title: A Tale of Two Walks: From Kac to KMP and Back
papers.abstract: We reveal an unexpected connection between two interacting particle systems: Kac's walk and the Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti (KMP) process. We first establish a mixing-time analogue of Aldous's conjecture for the KMP process on general graphs: the mixing time of the $t$-particle process on any connected $d$-vertex graph is at most $O(\log d)$ times the corresponding single-particle mixing time, uniformly in $t$. As an application, we improve the mixing-time bound for coordinate hit-and-run on the $n$-dimensional standard simplex from $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ [KV26] to $O(n\log n)$, while removing the dependence on the initial distribution. We then show that the twirling channel induced by the parallel Kac's walk on the symmetric subspace can be exactly encoded by a Markov chain on partitions, which naturally lifts to a parallel KMP chain on the complete graph. We prove that $O(\log d+\log(1/\varepsilon))$ repetitions of the parallel Kac's walk suffice to approximate Haar twirling on the symmetric subspace of $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes t}$ to error $\varepsilon$, uniformly in all $t$. Our main technical contribution is a new structural property of KMP-type dynamics: conditional product structure, which holds for both the standard KMP processes on general graphs and the parallel KMP processes on complete graphs. Conditioned on suitable auxiliary randomness, the evolution of the labeled KMP process factorizes into independent single-particle updates. Combining this structure with an exact coupling, we remove the dependence on the number of particles from the mixing bounds for both unlabeled KMP models. This bypasses the $\log(π_{\min}^{-1})$ dependency from spectral-gap arguments, which is often prohibitively large for many-particle systems. Using this framework, we prove mixing bounds that are sharp up to logarithmic factors for both unlabeled KMP models.

papers.title: Approximation of a continuous-variable Gaussian state by discrete-variable quantum states
papers.abstract: For every centered one-mode continuous-variable Gaussian state, we prove that the signed Wigner periodization defines a discrete-variable density operator in every odd dimension $d\ge3$. Positivity is equivalent to the one-mode uncertainty condition, and we determine the complete inertia outside and on its boundary. A covariance-independent isometric embedding gives exponential convergence in trace norm, with an explicit error bound uniform in Planck's constant. For covariance twice the identity, dimension $31$ gives a certified trace-norm error below $1/8000$. The trace-norm estimate controls all measurement probabilities. We retain the original canonical-coherent-frame formula in terms of the determinant and trace of the covariance matrix, with continuous normalization fixed to agree with the discrete frame convention. The coherence comparisons identify which diagnostics accompany the controlled state approximation. Position- and momentum-basis coherences have exponentially convergent values after division by the square root of the dimension. Numerical comparisons of purity and frame coherence illustrate the discrete-continuous transition.
papers.comments: Substantially revised and expanded, with new authors, title and abstract; added proofs of positivity and quantitative discrete-continuous approximation, and extended coherence comparisons

papers.title: Fast mixing of the SYK model at high temperatures
papers.abstract: The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model is a strongly interacting fermionic system. Its dynamics are difficult to analyze with Lieb-Robinson bounds and cluster expansions due to its all-to-all disordered interactions. We prove that, with high probability over the disorder, the SYK model admits a quantum Gibbs sampler with a system-size-independent spectral gap at sufficiently high constant temperatures. This yields polynomial-time preparation of SYK Gibbs states on a quantum computer. While prior non-rigorous computations that suggested SYK thermalization were limited to studying local correlators, we emphasize that our result holds up to arbitrary inverse polynomial trace distance. Our proof introduces the pseudo-Lindbladian approach to fermions then applies two key new ideas: a Bochner inequality for quantum dynamics, and an especially simple SYK analysis based on a comparison to classical dynamics.
papers.comments: 34 pages; v2 improves exposition and updates references

papers.title: An FPRAS for Counting Common Bases of Two Matroids
papers.abstract: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) for approximately counting and uniformly sampling common bases of two matroids given by their independence oracles. Moreover, our algorithms generalize far beyond this to Hadamard products of two probability measures on the Boolean cube satisfying a simple nonnegative curvature condition. These algorithmic primitives have myriad applications in statistical physics, polyhedral combinatorics, the theory of quantum many-body systems, and beyond. The central difficulty is that the hard constraints imposed by the two input matroids (or the two input measures, more generally) obstruct traditional approaches based on local Markov chains. Relaxing these constraints can restore rapid mixing, but configurations that satisfy the original hard constraints may become exponentially rare if this is done naïvely. Our main contribution is a novel approach for approximate counting that marries Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) with convex programming to overcome these obstacles: - We relax the intersection by imposing an overlap penalty on the product measure formed by the two input measures. We prove, via an integrated Bochner-type method, that this "soft intersection" satisfies a Poincaré Inequality uniformly over all external fields. - We use samples from the relaxed distribution to solve a dual maximum entropy convex program inspired by the Gurvits capacity. This program reweights the soft intersection measure using external fields to boost the aggregate probability of configurations satisfying the hard intersection constraint, without changing their relative weights. We bound the success probability directly using the uniform Poincaré Inequality and smallness of the gradient norm. AI Disclosure: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra and GPT-6 Astra Ultra were heavily used to develop the ideas in this paper.

papers.title: Improved Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir Secret Sharing and Worst-Case Optimal Polynomial Intersection
papers.abstract: We study two problems: Local Leakage Resilience (LLR) for Shamir secret sharing, and worst-case Optimal Polynomial Intersection (OPI), over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$. For a polynomial $Q(X)$ of degree less than $k$, LLR for Shamir secret sharing asks what a few leaked bits from each of the $n$ shares $Q(α_1), \ldots, Q(α_n)$ reveal about $Q(0)$. Given (worst-case) input lists $S_1, \ldots, S_n \subset \mathbb{F}_p$, OPI seeks a polynomial $Q(X)$ so that $Q(α_i) \in S_i$ for as many $i$ as possible. Leveraging recent connections between these two problems due to (Sun, Wootters 2026), we improve the state-of-the-art for both problems. For LLR, we show that there is some constant $δ> 0$ so that Shamir secret-sharing is one-bit LLR (only a negligible amount about $Q(0)$ is learned) whenever $R := k/n \geq 1/2 - δ$. This is the first result to break the so-called ``one-half barrier'' for LLR, and improves over the previous best known result, requiring $R \geq 0.668$ (Kasser, 2025). For OPI, we give a quantum algorithm that finds a polynomial $Q(X)$ that agrees with at least a $\mathsf{SCL}_ρ(R)-\varepsilon$ fraction of the lists, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, where $\mathsf{SCL}_ρ$ is the \emph{semicircle law} of (Jordan et al., 2025). This improves previous algorithmic (and existential) results of (Jo, 2026) and (Horinaga, Yamakawa, 2026). We also give further improved existential results for all OPI instances; and when the evaluation points $α_i$ are chosen at random, for every rate $R > 0$ we show that, with high probability, for worst-case $S_i$ there exists \emph{perfect} solution. Finally, we adapt the hardness result of (Yamakawa, Zhandry, 2024) to apply to OPI (rather than a folded version); this gives an unconditional separation between the quantum and classical hardness of OPI relative to a membership oracle.
papers.comments: 82 pages, 3 figures; v2 adds near-optimal OPI discrepancy for random Reed-Solomon codes

papers.title: QPTAS for Max Weight Independent Set in Graphs with Strongly Edge-Sublinear Separators
papers.abstract: A hereditary graph class has strongly edge-sublinear separators if, for some constant $0 \leqslant b < 1$, every graph in the class with $m$ edges admits a balanced separator of size $\mathcal O(m^b)$. We show that Max Weight Independent Set (MWIS) admits a deterministic quasipolynomial-time approximation scheme (QPTAS) on every such class. In particular, this applies to graphs excluding any fixed graph as an induced minor, by a separator theorem of Korhonen and Lokshtanov [SODA 2024]. Our theorem generalizes the QPTASes for axis-parallel rectangles [Adamaszek and Wiese, FOCS 2013] and polygons [Adamaszek, Har-Peled, and Wiese, JACM 2019], or equivalently for packing connected subgraphs of a planar graph [Pilipczuk, van Leeuwen, and Wiese, Algorithmica 2020]. It also generalizes the QPTAS for MWIS on hereditary classes with strongly sublinear separators measured in vertices [Dvořák, EJC 2018; Dvořák and Lahiri, ESA 2021], as well as the QPTASes for graphs excluding specific induced minors [Chudnovsky et al., arXiv 2025; Bonnet et al., SWAT 2026; Czyżewska et al., arXiv 2026].

papers.title: Marginal bunching for \textit{in situ} certification of multiparticle indistinguishability
papers.abstract: We propose an \textit{in situ} method for certifying the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in generic linear interferometers. For particles occupying distinct input ports, the method uses two-particle marginal bunching or anti-bunching probabilities to bound full multiparticle indistinguishability through Aldous' spectral gap theorem. For Haar-random unitary interferometers, the number of experimental runs required to estimate this bound to a prescribed precision, at fixed confidence, is polynomial in the particle number, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability over the choice of interferometer. Losses are incorporated without conditioning on particle survival. The method is particularly suited to certifying photon indistinguishability in large-scale interference experiments, including Boson Sampling experiments targeting quantum computational advantage.
papers.comments: 21 pages, 1 figure (in color); in this revision: new Section VI introduces a weighted series of subsets and a lower bound based on Aldous' spectral gap theorem, thus removing a connectivity bottleneck; updated fig1 is placed in Section VI

papers.title: A Linear Lower Bound for Convex Body Chasing in Every Norm
papers.abstract: We establish an $Ω(d)$ lower bound on the competitive ratio of convex body chasing in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with movement costs measured in any norm. Previously, the best known lower bound valid across all norms was $Ω(d^{1/6})$, established by Papazov (2023); stronger lower bounds were known for $\ell_p$ norms, where Bubeck, Klartag, Lee, Li, and Sellke (2019) had established a lower bound of $Ω(\max\{\sqrt{d}, d^{1-1/p}\})$. In particular, a linear lower bound was known only for the $\ell_\infty$ norm, realized by the standard construction of chasing faces of a hypercube. Our lower bound strictly improves on the prior universal and $\ell_p$ lower bounds for $p < \infty$ and shows that the functional Steiner point algorithm of Sellke (2023) - which has competitive ratio $O(d)$ - is asymptotically optimal for every norm. Our approach is based on the recursive construction of Bubeck, Coester, and Rabani (2023) for metrical service systems, which gives a lower bound of $Ω(r^2)$ for requests of size $O(r)$. We show that requests in their construction, each comprising a set of discrete points in a graph metric, can be mapped to the vertices of convex requests in a $(2r+1)$-dimensional $\ell_p$ vector space while approximately preserving movement costs up to a factor of $O(r)$; the general result then follows via Milman's (1985) quotient-of-a-subspace theorem.
papers.comments: Updates the previous version to extend the lower bound to all norms

papers.title: Perturbative Holonomy Potentials and Vacua in Chiral Supersymmetric Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We present a Wilsonian framework, globally controlled across the holonomy space, for determining the perturbative data governing the vacua of chiral supersymmetric gauge theories on a circle. This allows lifting the Intriligator--Seiberg classification of semiclassical vacua in 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ Chern--Simons-matter theories to $\RR^3\times S^1$. The framework is showcased by finding a rich set of vacuum sectors in a simple $\U(1)$ model and by reproducing on flat space the R-twisted reduction (first diagnosed on $S^3\times S^1$) of an $\SU(2)$ Maruyoshi--Song theory to the Gang--Yamazaki theory.
papers.comments: 5 pages, 2 pages supplemental material, an ancillary Mathematica notebook; accompanying letter to arXiv:2604.27066 [hep-th]

papers.title: Asymptotic Rank of Weighted Graph Tensors via Completely Positive Covers
papers.abstract: We give a conic upper bound on the asymptotic rank of every weighted graph tensor over every field. If $W$ is the logarithmic edge-weight matrix of its dimension matrix $Q$, then $$ \operatorname{MaxCut}(W)\le\log_2\operatorname{\widetilde R}_{\mathbb F}(\operatorname{WT}(Q))\le U_{\operatorname{CP}}^Δ(W). $$ Here $U_{\operatorname{CP}}^Δ(W)$ maximizes $\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}W_{i,j}P_{i,j}$ over nonnegative symmetric zero-diagonal matrices $P$ such that $J-2P$ is copositive and $P_{i,j}\le P_{i,k}+P_{k,j}$ for all distinct vertices. The matrix $J$ is all-one, and copositivity means nonnegativity of the quadratic form on nonnegative vectors. Our starting point extends OpenAI's polynomial multiplication method and its subsequent arbitrary-field developments from three tensor legs to arbitrary order. We prove $$ \left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor\le\log_2\operatorname{\widetilde R}_{\mathbb F}(\operatorname{GT}_2(K_n))\le\frac{n^2}{4}. $$ The edge exponent is at most $n/(2(n-1))$ and tends to the optimal value $1/2$, improving the previous Coppersmith--Winograd bounds and answering Question 1.3.1 of Christandl, Vrana, and Zuiddam. The bounds coincide for every even $n$. For every odd $m\ge3$, the theorem gives $\log_2\widetilde R_{\mathbb F}(\operatorname{GT}_2(C_m))\le m-1+1/(m+1)$, improving the previous cycle bound with a gap of only $1/(m+1)$ above the maximum cut. On weighted triangles, the program recovers the rectangular matrix multiplication curve of Uznański and Amanov, van den Berg, and Zuiddam. The CP and semidefinite programs, with or without path constraints, all have value $9/4$ on the unweighted triangle, giving this upper bound a natural conic interpretation. Further applications give explicit bounds for complete multipartite graphs, split graphs, and wheels, including new cases of maximum-cut equality.
papers.comments: 80 pages, 5 figures, abstract shortened to meet arXiv requirements

papers.title: Zero-freeness for Random Regular Graphs up to the Replica Symmetry Breaking Threshold
papers.abstract: We study antiferromagnetic spin systems on random regular graphs through the lens of the phase transitions characterized by the complex zeros of the partition function. Our motivating examples include the hardcore model and the antiferromagnetic Potts model (including proper $q$-colorings at $β=0$). For both models on random $d$-regular graphs, we establish, with high probability over the graph, zero-free regions throughout the interior of the replica-symmetric regime. Asymptotically, this regime extends up to tree occupation density $$α< α_{\mathrm{RSB}}(d) = (2\log d - 2\log\log d + 2 - 2\log 2 + o_d(1))/d$$ for the hardcore model and up to degree $$d < d_{\mathrm{RSB}}(q) = (2q-1)\log q - 2\log 2 + o_q(1)$$ for proper $q$-colorings. Leveraging the standard algorithmic implications of zero-freeness, we obtain deterministic polynomial-time algorithms that multiplicatively approximate the corresponding partition functions at fixed rational parameters throughout this regime, with high probability over the graph. Our algorithmic guarantees significantly improve upon prior work and extend beyond the parameter ranges reached by previously known search algorithms. As a key intermediate step, we establish the pointwise equivalence, away from the threshold, of three notions of replica symmetry: geometric (averaged pairwise correlation decay), thermodynamic (convergence to the Bethe free-energy prediction), and variational (nonpositivity of the Bethe functional). To establish zero-freeness, we develop reinforced small subgraph conditioning, lifting classical small subgraph conditioning to random holomorphic functions to control short-cycle fluctuations. We also use variational replica symmetry to obtain exponential planted overlap concentration. This enables a typical-graph truncation that controls complex second moments up to the replica symmetry breaking threshold.
papers.comments: Revised and expanded: strengthened the characterization of the replica-symmetric phase, reorganized and expanded the proofs. 84 pages

papers.title: Nearly-Optimal Time-Sample Trade-off in Consensus Dynamics
papers.abstract: How does the number of sampled opinions affect the time required to reach consensus in distributed consensus dynamics? We study the synchronous $h$-Majority, in which every node independently samples $h$ nodes uniformly at random with replacement in each round and adopts a most frequent sampled opinion, breaking ties uniformly at random. We show that $h$-Majority achieves the nearly-optimal trade-off between the sample size and the consensus time, among a broad class of consensus dynamics. In particular, we prove the following results. For every sample size $h \ge 3$ and for every initial configuration, we prove that the process reaches consensus with high probability within $$\widetilde{O}\left(1+\min\left\{\frac{1}{\min\{h^2p_{\max},1\}},\frac{\sqrt{n}}{h}\right\}\right)$$ rounds, where $n$ is the number of nodes and $p_{\max}$ is the largest initial fraction of nodes supporting any single opinion. This is the first bound on the consensus time for $h$-Majority that holds for every $h\ge3$ and every initial configuration. When the initially most popular opinion has a sufficiently large lead over every other opinion, we show that all nodes adopt this opinion with high probability within $O(\log n/\min\{h^2p_{\max},1\})$ rounds. We establish a matching lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors for any fixed update rule that treats all opinions symmetrically and that selects either a sampled opinion or the node's current opinion.

papers.title: Representation-Aware Closed-Surface Parameterization: Exact Sensitivity Analysis and Pole-Aware Planar Preconditioning
papers.abstract: Surface parameterization is a fundamental task in geometry processing and shape analysis. For topologically closed surfaces, it is common to parameterize them onto a standardized closed domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a prime example being a unit sphere for genus-0 closed surfaces. Many mapping methods use planar projections and perform computations on the plane rather than directly on the 3D surface. However, perturbations introduced before projection or geometric evolution propagate through the computation and may affect map quality, convergence, stopping behavior, and geometric validity. In this work, we formulate representation sensitivity as a branchwise input--output problem, separating smooth propagation through active Jacobians from changes in anchors, stopping rules, and fallback events. Under consistent piecewise-linear assembly, the unmodified south-pole Beltrami correction in the FLASH method for spherical conformal parameterization reduces exactly to source-mesh harmonic extension. On a fixed-anchor branch, the corrected map factors into chart transition, harmonic propagation, and inverse stereographic projection, yielding an explicit sensitivity Jacobian and a finite-triangle conditioning bound. Separately, we introduce a bounded five-parameter affine preconditioner over planar scale, translation, and anisotropy and evaluate candidates on the corrected spherical map. Across 30 genus-0 surfaces, it reduces median polar upper-tail log-condition and chord-angle distortion by $10.17\%$ and $10.97\%$, respectively, with both measures improving on every mesh. We also apply the framework to other spherical mapping methods including the conformalized mean-curvature flow and spherical density-equalizing maps. Altogether, our work highlights the importance of representation selection as a structural and practical component of spherical parameterization and downstream computation.

papers.title: Classical and Quantum Logics with Multiple Non-Equivalent and Non-Isomorphic Models
papers.abstract: Both quantum and classical logics have several mutually non-equivalent and non-isomorphic models as has repeatedly been proved in the literature. Yet, several authors have recently come with criticisms of this result. In this paper, we show that the criticisms are either unfounded or wrong.
